themes.definition: This question assesses whether judicial review detects and remedies inadequate counsel, withheld evidence, procedural failures, and unreliable death sentences before execution.

themes.name: Can comparative review and proportionality analysis prevent unequal death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether courts can identify excessive or inconsistent capital sentences by comparing defendants, offenses, jurisdictions, and similarly situated cases.

themes.name: Do empirical studies support the constitutional and policy legitimacy of the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether evidence about arbitrariness, discrimination, reliability, deterrence, and real-world administration justifies retaining or reforming capital punishment.

themes.name: Can incremental legal reforms make capital punishment fair enough to retain, or do systemic defects require abolition?
themes.definition: This question tests whether procedural and institutional reforms can overcome persistent arbitrariness, inequality, and legitimacy problems or whether those problems warrant suspension or abolition.

themes.name: Have post-Furman capital-sentencing schemes actually eliminated arbitrary and inconsistent death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether statutory standards, jury instructions, and appellate review meaningfully constrain discretion sufficiently to produce consistent death-penalty outcomes.

themes.name: Do aggravating-circumstance requirements meaningfully restrict death eligibility to the “worst of the worst” murders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether statutory narrowing distinguishes exceptionally aggravated murders from other death-eligible or otherwise serious killings.

themes.name: Does capital sentencing adequately individualize punishment according to a defendant’s culpability and the circumstances of the offense?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether death decisions reflect individualized responsibility rather than offense categories, generalized assumptions, or guilt-phase findings alone.

themes.name: Does race—especially the race of the victim and defendant—systematically influence capital charging, sentencing, or execution?
themes.definition: This question investigates racial disparities and racialized judgments at different stages of the death-penalty process.

themes.name: How do geography and local community characteristics affect death-penalty outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether county, state, regional, demographic, or political differences produce unequal likelihoods of capital charging, sentencing, or execution.

themes.name: Do capital cases adequately protect against wrongful convictions and wrongful executions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether trial procedures, evidentiary rules, post-conviction review, and heightened scrutiny reliably detect and prevent fatal errors.

themes.name: Does ineffective or under-resourced capital defense counsel undermine the reliability of death sentences?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether counsel’s preparation, investigation, presentation, and litigation performance meet constitutional and professional standards.

themes.name: Do professional standards such as the ABA Guidelines improve capital-defense investigation and mitigation practice?
themes.definition: This question tests whether formalized defense standards and professionalization produce better representation and more reliable sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: How should counsel’s mitigation duties apply when a capital defendant refuses, waives, or opposes mitigation?
themes.definition: This question addresses the conflict between defendant autonomy and counsel’s obligation to investigate and present evidence that could prevent a death sentence.

themes.name: How have courts implemented the Atkins prohibition on executing intellectually disabled defendants?
themes.definition: This question examines how state and federal courts define, prove, and review intellectual disability in post-conviction capital cases.

themes.name: Do mental illness, developmental disability, trauma, poverty, or other social conditions undermine a capital defendant’s perceived responsibility?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how mental-health and social-background evidence affects judgments of blameworthiness, mitigation, and eligibility for execution.

themes.name: Do capital juries make life-or-death decisions reliably and independently?
themes.definition: This question investigates how juror beliefs, moral and emotional commitments, deliberation, unanimity requirements, and interpersonal pressure shape sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: Does information beyond the legally defined facts of the crime bias capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question concerns the influence of character narratives, victim and defendant portrayals, community sentiment, emotion, and other extralegal information on death decisions.

themes.name: Should guilt and deathworthiness be decided through separate juries or otherwise distinct procedures?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether separating guilt-phase and penalty-phase decision-making improves individualized sentencing and reduces prejudicial carryover.

themes.name: Do restrictions on penalty-phase evidence and information compromise the reliability of capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question examines whether evidentiary exclusions, limited mitigation presentation, or sentencing instructions prevent decisionmakers from considering relevant individualized circumstances.

themes.name: Does appellate review meaningfully correct unjust or disproportionate death sentences?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether appellate and post-conviction courts detect differences in case worthiness, constitutional violations, attorney error, and unreliable sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: Are mandatory or defendant-requested death sentences compatible with individualized constitutional limits on capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether automatic death sentences or defendants’ autonomous requests for execution can satisfy requirements of individualized culpability and heightened reliability.

themes.name: Can empirical evidence establish that capital punishment deters murder or is otherwise necessary as a form of punishment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the strength and limits of deterrence and other consequentialist evidence used to justify the death penalty.

themes.name: Does the death penalty remain constitutionally legitimate under evolving standards of decency and proportionality?
themes.definition: This question considers whether contemporary societal judgments, disproportionality, cruelty, and the severity of execution support or undermine the continuing constitutionality of capital punishment.

themes.name: Can institutional and legal reforms make the administration of capital punishment sufficiently fair and legitimate?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether reforms, moratoriums, abolition efforts, or changes in federal-state administration can resolve systemic arbitrariness, discrimination, error, and implementation failures.

themes.name: Have post-Furman capital-sentencing reforms actually eliminated arbitrary and unequal outcomes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether reforms adopted after Furman and Gregg have produced more consistent, reliable, and evenhanded death-sentencing decisions.

themes.name: Does constitutional regulation make the death penalty sufficiently fair and reliable to remain legitimate?
themes.definition: This question examines whether Eighth, Fourteenth, and related constitutional safeguards adequately control the risks created by an irreversible punishment.

themes.name: Are capital-eligibility rules overinclusive or disproportionate under the Eighth Amendment?
themes.definition: This question asks whether statutory definitions of death-eligible crimes and defendants encompass people or offenses whose culpability does not justify execution.

themes.name: Can individualized mitigation be reconciled with consistency and equality in capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question examines whether considering each defendant’s circumstances produces individualized justice without creating unjustified disparities across comparable cases.

themes.name: Can capital juries apply legal standards consistently when making life-or-death decisions?
themes.definition: This question studies whether jurors understand and follow instructions governing culpability, mitigation, aggravation, and the choice between life and death.

themes.name: Does the jury’s weighing of aggravating and mitigating circumstances provide a meaningful constraint on death sentencing?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the formal weighing process genuinely structures sentencing or merely legitimizes largely discretionary moral judgments.

themes.name: Do racial and gender biases affect who is prosecuted, sentenced, or executed?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether defendant, victim, juror, or institutional characteristics produce unequal capital outcomes unrelated to legally relevant culpability.

themes.name: Does jury representativeness affect the fairness of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question asks whether exclusion or underrepresentation of particular racial and social groups changes capital juries’ judgments or undermines the legitimacy of their decisions.

themes.name: How do prosecutorial discretion and state-level procedural variation shape capital-sentencing disparities?
themes.definition: This question examines whether charging choices, local practices, and differing state statutory frameworks systematically influence who becomes death-eligible or receives a death sentence.

themes.name: Is capital defense representation sufficiently competent and resourced to produce reliable death-sentencing decisions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether counsel’s professional conditions, investigative resources, and performance adequately protect defendants facing execution.

themes.name: Can professional standards and institutional reforms correct structural deficiencies in capital defense lawyering?
themes.definition: This question asks whether changes in appointment systems, funding, training, and oversight can remedy recurring failures in capital representation.

themes.name: How should intellectual disability be determined when deciding whether a defendant may be executed?
themes.definition: This question assesses the validity, consistency, and legal consequences of psychological and clinical standards used to identify intellectual disability in capital cases.

themes.name: Should mental illness, youth, trauma, or social deprivation restrict capital punishment because they reduce culpability?
themes.definition: This question examines whether diminished-capacity conditions beyond intellectual disability should create categorical exemptions or otherwise limit death eligibility.

themes.name: Do appellate and postconviction procedures adequately prevent wrongful executions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether review mechanisms, newly developed evidence, and litigation strategies can detect and correct constitutional or factual errors after trial.

themes.name: Does the availability of life imprisonment alter jurors’ willingness to impose death?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether life-without-parole and related alternatives change capital juries’ evaluation of punishment, risk, and moral responsibility.

themes.name: How reliable are empirical studies used to evaluate capital punishment and guide its reform?
themes.definition: This question scrutinizes the methods, evidence, and inferential limits of research on capital sentencing, administration, consequences, and policy.

themes.name: Does the death penalty reduce homicide or otherwise achieve a measurable deterrent effect?
themes.definition: This question tests whether capital punishment produces crime-reduction benefits that distinguish it from alternative severe sanctions.

themes.name: Can retribution or desert morally justify state-authorized execution?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether imposing death is ethically warranted by the offender’s culpability and the seriousness of the offense.

themes.name: Can systemic defects in capital punishment be repaired incrementally, or do they require abolition?
themes.definition: This question compares procedural and administrative reform with abolition as responses to recurring structural unfairness and institutional failure.

themes.name: Do declining executions and infrequent use undermine the legitimacy or constitutional viability of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the rarity and uneven distribution of executions affect the punishment’s social meaning, legal status, or continued justification.

themes.name: Does the Eighth Amendment require capital sentencers to consider all relevant mitigating evidence about a defendant's background, character, and mental condition?
themes.definition: This question concerns the constitutional scope and practical adequacy of individualized mitigation in death-penalty sentencing.

themes.name: Can capital defense counsel reliably investigate and present mitigation evidence for indigent defendants?
themes.definition: This question examines whether funding, attorney-client relationships, multidisciplinary teams, and professional practices provide constitutionally adequate mitigation representation.

themes.name: How do jurors interpret narratives about a capital defendant's character, life history, and moral culpability?
themes.definition: This question studies how humanizing or condemning portrayals influence jurors' life-or-death sentencing judgments.

themes.name: Do juror predispositions and cultural beliefs produce an excessive willingness to impose death?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether attitudes toward capital punishment, extralegal beliefs, and psychological barriers bias capital sentencing decisions.

themes.name: Can jury procedures produce morally responsible and nonarbitrary capital sentencing decisions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether jury selection, instructions, deliberation, and penalty-phase procedures make jury-imposed death sentences fair and reliable.

themes.name: Does racial bias influence which defendants are prosecuted, sentenced, and selected for execution?
themes.definition: This question concerns racial and ethnic disparities arising from prosecutorial decisions, juror judgments, sentencing, and appellate administration.

themes.name: Are capital defendants treated differently because of extralegal characteristics unrelated to culpability or crime seriousness?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether race, poverty, politics, social status, or other legally irrelevant factors distort capital outcomes.

themes.name: Do capital-sentencing procedures adequately prevent arbitrary and inconsistent death sentences across cases and jurisdictions?
themes.definition: This question tests whether legal safeguards actually produce evenhanded outcomes rather than unpredictable or geographically uneven punishment.

themes.name: Does discretion by prosecutors, judges, and juries determine who receives death in ways that formal rules cannot control?
themes.definition: This question examines how institutional and case-specific discretion creates or prevents unequal capital-sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: Are aggravating circumstances and narrowing rules sufficiently precise to identify genuinely death-eligible defendants?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether eligibility standards meaningfully narrow the class of defendants who may be sentenced to death.

themes.name: Should the death penalty be limited to defendants who are individually among the most culpable and deserving of execution?
themes.definition: This question concerns substantive proportionality and whether severe impairments, personal circumstances, or limited culpability constitutionally bar execution.

themes.name: Does comparative proportionality require similarly culpable offenders to receive similar capital punishments?
themes.definition: This question examines whether cross-case comparison can identify excessive, anomalous, or disproportionate death sentences.

themes.name: Do childhood trauma, developmental immaturity, mental illness, or diminished capacity make execution constitutionally disproportionate?
themes.definition: This question addresses how individual impairments and life circumstances affect death eligibility and the moral legitimacy of execution.

themes.name: Do inadequate resources and institutional failures make capital convictions and sentences insufficiently reliable?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether poor defense representation, deficient investigation, and systemic breakdowns increase erroneous or unfair capital outcomes.

themes.name: Are heightened procedural safeguards necessary because capital proceedings risk wrongful execution?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the death penalty's finality requires stronger review, evidence-development, and error-prevention procedures than ordinary criminal cases.

themes.name: Does post-conviction access to witnesses and newly discovered evidence effectively uncover wrongful capital convictions?
themes.definition: This question examines whether procedural barriers and available review mechanisms permit reliable correction of capital-case error.

themes.name: Has Supreme Court Eighth Amendment doctrine made capital punishment reliable and fair in actual practice?
themes.definition: This question compares constitutional doctrine since Furman with empirical evidence about how capital sentencing operates.

themes.name: Should categorical constitutional rules replace case-by-case review of recurring capital-sentencing defects?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether systemic problems require categorical limits rather than individualized judicial correction.

themes.name: Can legal and institutional reforms make the death penalty sufficiently fair and nonarbitrary to retain?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether procedural, professional, and legislative reforms can remedy persistent defects in capital punishment.

themes.name: Should capital punishment be abolished if constitutional safeguards cannot ensure its reliable and evenhanded administration?
themes.definition: This question links the empirical failure of regulation to the broader policy and moral permissibility of retaining the death penalty.

themes.name: Do formal capital-sentencing safeguards actually reduce arbitrary and inconsistent death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether guided-discretion rules, statutory standards, and other formal procedures produce reliable and consistent outcomes rather than merely appearing to constrain arbitrariness.

themes.name: Does systemic racial bias make the death penalty constitutionally or morally impermissible even without proof of intentional discrimination?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether statistical and institutional evidence of racial disparities is sufficient to challenge capital punishment when the law requires evidence of purposeful discrimination.

themes.name: How do race and perceptions of Black criminal threat influence capital-sentencing decisions?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether racialized assumptions about defendants, victims, and dangerousness affect charging, sentencing, or judgments about who deserves execution.

themes.name: Does geographic and jurisdictional variation make the administration of the death penalty arbitrary?
themes.definition: This question tests whether differences among states, counties, courts, or prosecutors cause similarly situated defendants to face substantially different risks of death sentences or execution.

themes.name: Does prosecutorial discretion produce unequal or arbitrary capital-sentencing outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines how prosecutors’ decisions to seek death, negotiate pleas, or pursue life sentences shape disparities that cannot be explained by legally relevant case characteristics.

themes.name: Do aggravating-factor requirements meaningfully narrow death eligibility to the most culpable offenders?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether statutory aggravators genuinely distinguish death-eligible murders from cases that warrant a noncapital sentence or life imprisonment.

themes.name: Can individualized sentencing reconcile jury discretion with consistent application of the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether allowing juries to make individualized moral judgments inevitably conflicts with the need for equal and predictable sentencing.

themes.name: Does mitigation evidence about trauma, deprivation, childhood, or psychological impairment reliably affect capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether comprehensive evidence about defendants’ life histories and impairments is meaningfully considered when juries choose between death and life imprisonment.

themes.name: Do defendants’ mental functioning and developmental limitations justify categorical restrictions or individualized mitigation of execution?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether intellectual, psychological, behavioral, or developmental characteristics should bar execution or reduce culpability in capital cases.

themes.name: Does the quality of capital defense counsel materially determine whether death sentences are imposed or upheld?
themes.definition: This question examines whether inadequate investigation, preparation, mitigation presentation, or strategic decision-making by defense teams undermines the fairness and reliability of capital proceedings.

themes.name: Do appellate and post-conviction courts meaningfully correct disproportionate or unreliable death sentences?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether review of trial error, counsel performance, and sentencing proportionality provides an effective remedy for arbitrary capital outcomes.

themes.name: Should empirical evidence about jurors’ actual decision-making shape constitutional rules for capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question tests whether research on juror attitudes, comprehension, emotions, and reasoning should alter legal assumptions about how capital juries evaluate evidence and law.

themes.name: How do courtroom narratives, emotions, and juror empathy affect the choice between execution and life imprisonment?
themes.definition: This question investigates how trial presentation, victim and defendant narratives, compassion, and moral emotions influence capital sentencing beyond formally specified facts.

themes.name: Does legally authorized evidence and expert testimony introduce unacceptable subjectivity into capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether psychological, psychiatric, scientific, or behavioral evidence produces unreliable judgments about dangerousness, culpability, or eligibility for death.

themes.name: Does post-Furman constitutional regulation adequately prevent arbitrary and capricious death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether modern Supreme Court doctrine and state procedures have resolved the constitutional problems identified in Furman v. Georgia.

themes.name: How much responsibility should the Supreme Court bear for constraining unequal state capital-punishment practices?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the Supreme Court’s role in defining, enforcing, and revising constitutional limits on state discretion in death-penalty cases.

themes.name: Can procedural reform make the death penalty reliable and legitimate, or do systemic flaws require abolition?
themes.definition: This question compares case-specific safeguards and institutional reforms with the argument that persistent error, bias, and arbitrariness are inherent reasons to eliminate capital punishment.

themes.name: Is the death penalty morally and legally justified despite state-inflicted violence, irreversible error, and unequal administration?
themes.definition: This question weighs retributive, rights-based, human-dignity, and anti-cruelty arguments for and against state-imposed execution.

themes.name: Does the death penalty deter homicide more effectively than a noncapital life sentence?
themes.definition: This question examines whether fear of execution provides a demonstrable deterrent benefit that can justify capital punishment over life imprisonment.

themes.name: What explains the gap between formal death sentences and actual executions?
themes.definition: This question investigates how appeals, delays, moratoriums, institutional resistance, and other legal or political factors prevent many death sentences from resulting in execution.

themes.name: Do post-Furman capital-sentencing procedures adequately constrain discretion to prevent arbitrary and capricious death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether statutory aggravating factors, sentencing standards, and procedural safeguards reliably limit life-or-death discretion.

themes.name: Does individualized consideration of culpability make capital sentencing more reliable without reintroducing arbitrariness?
themes.definition: This question assesses the constitutional and practical tension between tailoring punishment to each defendant and achieving consistent sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: Can empirical evidence demonstrate that capital sentencing is unconstitutionally arbitrary?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether statistical variation in death sentences can establish legally actionable arbitrariness rather than merely ordinary sentencing disagreement.

themes.name: Do racial and socioeconomic disparities undermine the constitutional legitimacy of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether race, poverty, or related demographic inequalities systematically influence death-penalty decisions in legally impermissible ways.

themes.name: Does geographic variation make the death penalty an unequal and arbitrary punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether differences among states, counties, prosecutors, or local institutions determine death-penalty outcomes more than the facts of the offense.

themes.name: How strongly does prosecutorial discretion determine who faces or receives a death sentence?
themes.definition: This question studies whether prosecutors’ charging and plea-seeking decisions produce substantial and potentially unjustified variation in capital punishment.

themes.name: Does inadequate defense representation prevent capital defendants from receiving a fair opportunity to avoid execution?
themes.definition: This question examines how counsel quality, funding, workload, and professional standards affect investigation, mitigation, sentencing, and post-conviction protection.

themes.name: Can post-conviction review reliably correct failures by capital defense counsel?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether collateral review procedures meaningfully remedy deficient representation and erroneous death sentences after trial.

themes.name: Does mitigating evidence about a defendant’s background and life history materially change capital sentencing outcomes?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether childhood trauma, social context, family history, and other humanizing evidence persuade sentencers to impose life rather than death.

themes.name: How should mental illness, intellectual disability, and developmental impairment affect capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether psychological and functional impairments should reduce culpability, bar execution, or otherwise alter the legal treatment of capital defendants.

themes.name: Does the legal system reliably translate psychiatric and psychological evidence into capital-sentencing judgments?
themes.definition: This question examines the evidentiary and conceptual difficulties involved in converting mental-health assessments into findings about responsibility, dangerousness, or death-worthiness.

themes.name: Does youth or developmental immaturity make execution constitutionally disproportionate?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether adolescents’ reduced maturity and greater capacity for change require categorical or individualized limits on capital punishment.

themes.name: Do jurors make individualized and consistent decisions about who deserves death?
themes.definition: This question studies how juror beliefs, moral judgments, narratives, and interpretation of aggravating and mitigating evidence shape life-or-death verdicts.

themes.name: Do competing narratives about defendants and crimes distort capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question examines whether character portrayals, contextual stories, and dehumanizing or humanizing descriptions cause legally irrelevant perceptions to influence punishment.

themes.name: Does the combination of guilt-phase and penalty-phase strategies affect the fairness of capital trials?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether bifurcated proceedings create strategic conflicts or opportunities that influence both conviction and sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: Can proportionality review ensure that similarly culpable offenders receive similar capital punishments?
themes.definition: This question assesses how courts define comparable cases and whether comparative review can identify excessive, inconsistent, or disproportionate death sentences.

themes.name: Are courts and legislatures effective in correcting defective capital-sentencing systems?
themes.definition: This question compares the capacity of judicial review, statutory reform, and institutional intervention to remedy unconstitutional or unreliable death-penalty practices.

themes.name: Does Supreme Court constitutional doctrine meaningfully constrain the administration of the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question examines whether evolving Eighth Amendment standards and empirical-evidence requirements produce practical limits on state capital procedures.

themes.name: Do wrongful convictions and wrongful executions make the death penalty irredeemably unreliable?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the risk of irreversible error can be reduced through safeguards or instead defeats the legitimacy of capital punishment altogether.

themes.name: Can capital punishment be reformed into a fair, reliable, and nondiscriminatory system, or does it require abolition?
themes.definition: This question weighs whether procedural and institutional reforms can resolve documented defects or whether those defects are inherent in state-imposed execution.

themes.name: Have post-Furman and post-Gregg reforms actually eliminated arbitrary death sentences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether guided-discretion statutes, aggravating factors, jury instructions, and related reforms have made capital sentencing sufficiently rational, consistent, and non-arbitrary.

themes.name: Does the Eighth Amendment permit capital punishment when its administration remains inconsistent or disproportionate?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the constitutional ban on cruel, unusual, and disproportionate punishment limits the death penalty because of systemic arbitrariness rather than only because of specific execution methods or offender categories.

themes.name: Do statutory aggravating factors and jury instructions meaningfully constrain capital-sentencing discretion?
themes.definition: This question asks whether formal legal criteria actually guide jurors and judges toward legally authorized decisions instead of merely disguising subjective moral judgments.

themes.name: Does race influence capital sentencing through the race of the victim, defendant, or both?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether racialized patterns—especially victim-race and defendant-race effects—change the likelihood of a death sentence after accounting for legally relevant case characteristics.

themes.name: Do racial-disparity remedies adequately address constitutionally impermissible death sentences?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether courts provide meaningful relief when empirical evidence shows race-influenced charging, sentencing, or execution decisions.

themes.name: Does prosecutorial discretion produce geographically arbitrary death-penalty outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether county-level charging practices, political incentives, and local institutional cultures create large punishment differences among otherwise similar cases.

themes.name: How does death qualification affect juror bias and the reliability of capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether excluding jurors opposed to capital punishment produces juries that are systematically more conviction-prone, pro-death, or less receptive to mitigation.

themes.name: Can capital jurors reliably decide between life and death under legally prescribed standards?
themes.definition: This question tests whether jurors’ moral, emotional, and factual judgments in the penalty phase conform to statutory requirements rather than sentiment, stereotypes, or unstructured intuition.

themes.name: Does individualized mitigation meaningfully reduce death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether evidence about a defendant’s background, character, trauma, mental condition, and culpability changes sentencing outcomes rather than being overshadowed by the crime narrative.

themes.name: Do social and cultural stereotypes undermine the mitigating force of capital-defense evidence?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether race, class, gender, or other stereotypes cause decision-makers to discount humanizing and psychosocial evidence about defendants.

themes.name: What level of attorney performance is constitutionally required during the capital penalty phase?
themes.definition: This question concerns the legal standard for ineffective assistance of counsel, particularly counsel’s duties to investigate, develop, and present mitigating evidence.

themes.name: Do indigent capital defendants receive defense representation capable of producing reliable sentencing outcomes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether appointment systems, funding, workload, expertise, and institutional support allow capital defenders to provide competent representation.

themes.name: How should courts treat capital defendants who resist or complicate conventional defense strategies?
themes.definition: This question examines the tension between defendants’ autonomy and counsel’s protective duties when defendants oppose mitigation, waive appeals, or otherwise undermine standard defense approaches.

themes.name: Should mental illness or intellectual disability categorically restrict eligibility for execution?
themes.definition: This question asks how constitutional law should distinguish culpable capital offenders from defendants whose mental impairments undermine responsibility or make execution impermissible.

themes.name: Can capital-sentencing systems reliably identify the 'worst of the worst' offenders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether legal classifications of heinousness, aggravation, and culpability successfully distinguish death-eligible murderers from similarly situated defendants who receive lesser punishment.

themes.name: Do formal capital-sentencing rules translate into consistent real-world outcomes?
themes.definition: This question compares legal doctrine and courtroom practice to determine whether institutional actors apply prescribed criteria consistently across cases and jurisdictions.

themes.name: Are appellate, habeas, and post-conviction procedures adequate to prevent wrongful executions?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether review mechanisms detect factual error, incompetent representation, procedural violations, and arbitrary sentencing before an execution occurs.

themes.name: Do institutional failures, rather than isolated mistakes, cause unjust capital outcomes?
themes.definition: This question investigates how courts, prosecutors, defense systems, juries, prison authorities, and other institutions collectively produce or fail to correct unreliable death sentences.

themes.name: How do political incentives shape the adoption, administration, and review of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether electoral pressures, legislative strategy, executive authority, and abolitionist or retentionist advocacy distort decisions about charging, sentencing, appeals, and executions.

themes.name: Is abolition preferable to incremental reform of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question compares the moral, constitutional, and practical case for eliminating the death penalty with the possibility that procedural, legislative, and professional reforms can make it legitimate and reliable.

themes.name: Have post-Furman and post-Gregg reforms actually eliminated arbitrary and inconsistent death sentencing?
themes.definition: This question examines whether guided-discretion statutes, sentencing procedures, and appellate review have meaningfully constrained arbitrary variation in capital outcomes.

themes.name: Do capital-sentencing systems impose death sentences for reasons unrelated to culpability or the underlying offense?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether legally irrelevant factors, institutional practices, or decision-maker discretion influence death sentences beyond the defendant’s crime and blameworthiness.

themes.name: Does capital punishment produce racial disparities after accounting for offense severity and other relevant case characteristics?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether race affects charging, sentencing, or execution outcomes when appropriate underlying-case denominators and legally relevant controls are used.

themes.name: Do county prosecutors and local institutions explain geographic disparities in the use of the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question studies whether differences among counties, prosecutors, courts, and jurisdictions produce unequal patterns of capital charging and sentencing.

themes.name: Are constitutional and procedural safeguards sufficient to prevent wrongful capital convictions and executions?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether the capital system reliably detects factual error and prevents innocent or improperly convicted defendants from being sentenced to death or executed.

themes.name: Does inadequate defense representation make capital sentencing less accurate and less fair?
themes.definition: This question examines how attorney competence, funding, investigation, expert assistance, and defense-team resources affect capital-case outcomes.

themes.name: Does death qualification bias juries toward conviction and death sentences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether excluding jurors unwilling to impose the death penalty produces unrepresentative juries or systematically harsher verdicts and sentences.

themes.name: Can jury-based capital sentencing produce reliable and non-arbitrary judgments about who should live or die?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether jurors can consistently apply capital-sentencing standards while making reliable factual, moral, and punishment decisions.

themes.name: Does individualized sentencing improve justice, or does it increase inconsistency in capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines the tension between considering each defendant’s circumstances and maintaining proportional, evenhanded outcomes among similarly situated cases.

themes.name: Do mitigating evidence and humanizing accounts meaningfully reduce death sentences for defendants with diminished culpability?
themes.definition: This question studies how courts and juries evaluate mental illness, trauma, developmental history, family context, and other evidence offered in mitigation.

themes.name: Should categorical exemptions bar execution of defendants with intellectual disability, severe mental disorder, or other heightened vulnerabilities?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legal and normative justification for excluding especially vulnerable or less culpable offenders from capital punishment.

themes.name: Do capital-sentencing statutes adequately limit death eligibility to the most serious offenses and the most culpable offenders?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether statutory aggravating factors and proportionality rules sufficiently distinguish death-eligible murders from other homicide cases.

themes.name: Does the Eighth Amendment constitutionally prohibit capital punishment when its administration is arbitrary, disproportionate, or unreliable?
themes.definition: This question examines whether systemic defects in capital sentencing make the death penalty inconsistent with constitutional limits on cruel and unusual punishment.

themes.name: Has Supreme Court regulation meaningfully improved the fairness and reliability of state capital-sentencing systems?
themes.definition: This question analyzes whether Supreme Court doctrine, including the interpretation of Furman and Gregg, has effectively corrected systemic defects in state death-penalty administration.

themes.name: Are post-conviction review and clemency mechanisms capable of correcting errors in capital cases?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether procedural deadlines, judicial barriers, evidentiary restrictions, and institutional practices provide meaningful relief for unjust death sentences.

themes.name: Do execution methods and death-row procedures create unconstitutional risks of cruel and unusual punishment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the physical methods, delays, conditions, and administration of execution expose prisoners to impermissible pain, suffering, or psychological harm.

themes.name: Is capital punishment morally and legally justified by retribution, desert, or deterrence?
themes.definition: This question weighs competing claims that execution is justified as deserved punishment, crime prevention, or neither despite its irreversible character.

themes.name: Can procedural reform make the death penalty sufficiently rational and fair, or are its defects structural and irreparable?
themes.definition: This question tests whether improved rules and safeguards can remedy capital punishment’s recurring arbitrariness, error, and inequality without abolishing it.

themes.name: Why does documented unfairness and brutality fail to produce abolition or substantial restriction of the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question examines how political incentives, public opinion, institutional interests, and social conflict sustain capital punishment despite evidence against its legitimacy.

themes.name: Does empirical evidence credibly demonstrate that capital punishment is arbitrary, discriminatory, or unreliable?
themes.definition: This question assesses the methods, data, denominators, and inferential standards used to evaluate death-penalty administration and to support legal or policy reform.

themes.name: Have post-Furman reforms actually eliminated arbitrary and capricious death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether modern sentencing statutes, guidelines, and procedural rules meaningfully constrain discretion and produce reliable, nonarbitrary capital-sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: Can capital sentencing reconcile individualized consideration with consistency across comparable cases?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether decision-makers can account for each defendant’s culpability and circumstances without producing unjustified variation between similar cases.

themes.name: How do race, race of the victim, and socioeconomic status affect death-penalty outcomes?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether racial and class disparities influence charging, sentencing, or execution decisions, including through cross-racial empathic deficits and race-of-victim effects.

themes.name: Do death-qualified juries produce reliable and impartial capital-sentencing decisions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether juror qualification procedures, attitudes toward the death penalty, and juror characteristics distort judgments about guilt, culpability, mitigation, or punishment.

themes.name: How do jurors’ moral judgments and narrative perceptions of defendants influence capital sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines how culturally situated judgments about character, dangerousness, remorse, and culpability affect jurors’ life-or-death decisions beyond legally specified evidence.

themes.name: Are mitigation investigations and presentations sufficient to support individualized capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether defense teams adequately investigate and present psychological, developmental, family, social-history, and other mitigating evidence before a death sentence is imposed.

themes.name: Does ineffective capital defense counsel increase the risk of unreliable or excessive death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether inadequate appointment, investigation, preparation, or advocacy by counsel materially affects capital-case outcomes and constitutional reliability.

themes.name: Should youth, intellectual disability, or severe mental illness categorically bar execution?
themes.definition: This question considers whether diminished cognitive or developmental capacity sufficiently reduces culpability to make execution constitutionally or morally impermissible.

themes.name: How do prosecutorial discretion and geographic variation shape who receives the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether prosecutors, local political incentives, and jurisdiction-specific practices produce substantial differences in capital charging and sentencing.

themes.name: Can appellate, habeas, and post-conviction review reliably correct questionable death sentences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether later-stage judicial review identifies and remedies legal error, inadequate representation, unreliable evidence, or excessive punishment before execution.

themes.name: Do prolonged death-row delays violate constitutional limits on harsh punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether lengthy delays between sentencing and execution, including institutional backlogs and repeated review, make continued incarceration or execution constitutionally impermissible.

themes.name: Are heightened procedural safeguards necessary because capital punishment is uniquely severe and final?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether capital cases require protections beyond ordinary criminal proceedings to prevent irreversible and unconstitutional outcomes.

themes.name: Can proportionality review distinguish constitutionally excessive death sentences from permissible ones?
themes.definition: This question examines whether courts can meaningfully compare offenses and punishments to prevent death sentences that are disproportionate to the defendant’s culpability or crime.

themes.name: Does the legal system reliably distinguish death-eligible defendants from those who should receive life imprisonment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether statutory eligibility rules and sentencing procedures identify the narrow class of offenders who are sufficiently culpable for execution.

themes.name: Do Supreme Court standards adequately regulate state capital-sentencing systems?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether constitutional doctrine, including Eighth Amendment rules and national-consensus analysis, provides clear and enforceable limits on state discretion.

themes.name: Should systemic defects in capital punishment lead to abolition rather than incremental reform?
themes.definition: This question weighs whether persistent arbitrariness, discrimination, error, and institutional failure can be remedied through procedural changes or instead require ending the death penalty.

themes.name: Is capital punishment morally and legally legitimate apart from deterrence-based justifications?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether retribution, desert, state authority, and other conventional rationales adequately justify execution in light of its human and institutional consequences.

themes.name: Does the death penalty remain legitimate when its administration is unequal or empirically unreliable?
themes.definition: This question asks whether real-world disparities, mistaken sentences, and departures from formal legal rules undermine the constitutional and moral validity of capital punishment.

themes.name: Does the risk of executing innocent or undeserving defendants defeat the justification for capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether wrongful convictions, unreliable evidence, and failures to identify nonculpable defendants make the irreversible penalty unacceptable.

themes.name: Can life imprisonment serve as an adequate alternative when a death sentence is uncertain or unjust?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether noncapital sanctions preserve public safety and punishment goals while avoiding the irreversibility and error risks of execution.

themes.name: Does individualized mitigation evidence make capital sentencing more reliable and constitutionally legitimate?
themes.definition: This question examines whether defendants’ life histories, childhood trauma, and other mitigating circumstances meaningfully improve individualized judgments about culpability and punishment.

themes.name: Do capital jurors understand and properly weigh mitigating evidence when choosing between death and life imprisonment?
themes.definition: This question focuses on jurors’ comprehension, interpretation, and use of mitigation during the penalty phase.

themes.name: How do juror composition, attitudes, and extralegal beliefs influence death-sentencing decisions?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether demographic characteristics, punitive attitudes, or courtroom influences bias juries toward imposing death.

themes.name: Does victim impact evidence improperly influence the severity of capital sentences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether information about victims and their families produces unequal or constitutionally problematic sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: Does race influence who is prosecuted for, sentenced to, or executed for a capital offense?
themes.definition: This question examines racial disparities associated with defendants, victims, prosecutors, jurisdictions, and other stages of capital-punishment administration.

themes.name: Can formally race-neutral capital procedures prevent racialized outcomes?
themes.definition: This question tests whether statutory reforms, proportionality review, and institutional safeguards effectively address disparities without explicitly considering race.

themes.name: How do prosecutorial, judicial, and institutional discretion produce racial or geographic disparities in capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question studies how discretionary decisions and local institutional contexts affect the selection and disposition of capital cases.

themes.name: Do decentralized state and local institutions make capital punishment inconsistent across jurisdictions?
themes.definition: This question investigates the effects of regional variation, local politics, fiscal conditions, and administrative practices on capital outcomes.

themes.name: Did post-Furman reforms successfully replace arbitrary capital sentencing with genuinely guided discretion?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether aggravating-factor schemes and other statutory reforms meaningfully constrain life-or-death decision-making.

themes.name: Do modern capital-sentencing procedures actually prevent arbitrary and inconsistent death verdicts?
themes.definition: This question compares formal procedural safeguards with the real-world consistency, reviewability, and predictability of capital decisions.

themes.name: Are capital defendants constitutionally entitled to greater procedural safeguards than defendants facing ordinary imprisonment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the irreversibility and severity of death require heightened standards for evidence, participation, adjudication, and review.

themes.name: Does inadequate defense counsel undermine the reliability of capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether deficient counsel, insufficient investigation, or inadequate defense-team resources distort penalty-phase outcomes.

themes.name: Can trial, appellate, and post-conviction review reliably detect and correct wrongful capital convictions and sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines the effectiveness of legal review mechanisms in identifying serious factual, procedural, and constitutional errors before execution.

themes.name: Do AEDPA and other procedural barriers prevent federal courts from correcting unconstitutional capital cases?
themes.definition: This question focuses on how habeas restrictions and demanding evidentiary rules affect federal review and remedies in death-penalty litigation.

themes.name: Should people with intellectual disabilities or serious cognitive impairments be categorically excluded from capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines how mental capacity, diagnostic standards, and evolving constitutional principles limit execution eligibility.

themes.name: Are death sentences reserved for the most culpable offenders and the most serious crimes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether capital punishment is proportionate to individual responsibility, offense severity, and legally relevant aggravating circumstances.

themes.name: Is life imprisonment without parole a constitutionally and morally preferable alternative to death?
themes.definition: This question compares death sentences with life-without-parole sentences in terms of proportionality, punishment severity, legitimacy, and sentencing choice.

themes.name: Does the allocation of authority among judges, juries, prosecutors, and governors affect the fairness of capital sentencing and execution?
themes.definition: This question investigates how institutional responsibility and decision-making power shape life-or-death outcomes.

themes.name: Do capital-case narratives and courtroom presentations humanize defendants enough to support legitimate punishment decisions?
themes.definition: This question examines how storytelling, defendant characterization, and presentation of personal history influence moral judgments about execution.

themes.name: Does empirical evidence support the deterrence rationale for capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether death-penalty data demonstrate a deterrent effect on murder and whether such evidence bears on the punishment’s legitimacy.

themes.name: Do discretionary capital-sentencing systems impose death on defendants who are not clearly among the most aggravated offenders?
themes.definition: This question examines whether prosecutorial, jury, and judicial discretion produces overinclusive, disproportionate, or arbitrary death sentences rather than reserving execution for the worst cases.

themes.name: Do constitutional safeguards meaningfully prevent arbitrary and discriminatory death sentences in practice?
themes.definition: This question compares formal Eighth Amendment and statutory protections with the way capital-sentencing rules actually operate in courts and institutions.

themes.name: Does racial bias affect capital charging, sentencing, and execution decisions?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether defendant race, victim race, or broader racialized institutional practices produce unequal capital-punishment outcomes.

themes.name: Can statistical evidence establish systemic racial discrimination in capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legal and empirical usefulness of disparity studies and statistical proof in demonstrating racial bias in capital charging or sentencing.

themes.name: Does prosecutorial discretion determine which homicide defendants face the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question examines how prosecutors select capital cases and whether charging practices create unjustified disparities in death sentences.

themes.name: Do statutory aggravating factors and jury instructions adequately structure capital-sentencing discretion?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether legally defined aggravators and sentencing instructions reliably distinguish death-eligible cases from those warranting life imprisonment.

themes.name: Do capital juries make reliable and legally permissible individualized moral judgments?
themes.definition: This question studies how juror bias, psychological processes, group deliberation, and institutional design affect life-or-death sentencing decisions.

themes.name: Does the composition of capital juries satisfy constitutional requirements for fair and representative decision-making?
themes.definition: This question examines whether jury-selection practices and the exclusion of certain jurors undermine Sixth Amendment or related constitutional protections.

themes.name: Does the availability and disclosure of life without parole affect the fairness of death-sentence decisions?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether jurors must be informed about, and meaningfully consider, life imprisonment without parole as an alternative to execution.

themes.name: Do defense teams provide constitutionally adequate investigation and presentation in capital cases?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether appointed counsel and broader defense teams meet the heightened professional demands of capital litigation.

themes.name: Does mitigation evidence about a defendant’s life history, trauma, and family circumstances produce more reliable sentencing decisions?
themes.definition: This question examines whether humanizing and contextual evidence appropriately affects individualized judgments between death and life imprisonment.

themes.name: Should mental illness, intellectual disability, or developmental impairment categorically exclude a defendant from execution?
themes.definition: This question addresses the constitutional and moral limits on executing defendants whose cognitive or psychological conditions weaken culpability or reliability.

themes.name: Are death sentences proportionate to the culpability of defendants and the severity of comparable offenses?
themes.definition: This question examines whether capital punishment is imposed consistently across similarly situated defendants and cases.

themes.name: Do victim characteristics improperly influence capital charging and sentencing?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether the race, status, or social identity of a homicide victim affects the likelihood of a death sentence in ways unrelated to legally relevant culpability.

themes.name: Does geography produce unjustified variation in capital charging, sentencing, or execution?
themes.definition: This question studies whether jurisdictional differences and local institutional practices make the death penalty depend excessively on location.

themes.name: Can appellate, habeas, and post-conviction review correct unconstitutional or erroneous capital sentences before execution?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether post-trial legal procedures effectively identify and remedy constitutional violations, unreliable verdicts, and wrongful convictions.

themes.name: Does the risk of executing innocent people undermine the legitimacy of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether wrongful convictions, exonerations, and systemic trial failures provide a sufficient basis for rejecting or suspending executions.

themes.name: Does Supreme Court capital-punishment doctrine provide coherent and effective limits on state sentencing practices?
themes.definition: This question examines the consistency, empirical grounding, and practical consequences of Supreme Court regulation of capital eligibility, procedure, and arbitrariness.

themes.name: Can legal and institutional reforms make capital punishment meaningfully fairer and more reliable, or is abolition preferable?
themes.definition: This question compares reformist strategies such as heightened safeguards and narrowed eligibility with the argument that structural defects make the death penalty irredeemable.

themes.name: Are the moral and penological justifications for capital punishment—such as retribution, deterrence, and incapacitation—empirically and normatively defensible?
themes.definition: This question tests whether the claimed purposes of execution justify its severity and irreversibility under actual social and institutional conditions.

themes.name: Do post-Furman constitutional safeguards actually reduce arbitrariness in capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question examines whether modern eligibility rules, sentencing procedures, and appellate safeguards produce consistent and reliable outcomes rather than merely formal compliance with constitutional doctrine.

themes.name: Can aggravating-factor and eligibility rules reliably reserve the death penalty for the worst murders and most culpable offenders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether statutory narrowing mechanisms distinguish genuinely death-eligible cases from the broader population of murder cases without creating arbitrary or overinclusive classifications.

themes.name: Does individualized consideration of mitigation make capital sentencing more reliable and constitutionally legitimate?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether requiring sentencers to consider a defendant’s personal history, mental capacity, development, and offense context improves individualized judgments about death or mercy.

themes.name: Does legally structured discretion create unequal or unpredictable death sentences among similarly situated defendants?
themes.definition: This question analyzes how prosecutorial, judicial, and jury discretion generates disparities that cannot be explained by differences in offense seriousness or culpability.

themes.name: How does county-level prosecutorial discretion produce geographic disparities in capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether local charging practices and institutional cultures explain variation in death-sentence rates across counties and states.

themes.name: How do race, racial geography, and social status influence capital-sentencing decisions?
themes.definition: This question tests whether defendants’ or victims’ race, segregation patterns, and related status characteristics affect charging, sentencing, or execution decisions.

themes.name: Do jurors’ racial and moral biases undermine the fairness of capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question examines how jurors’ perceptions of race, remorse, dangerousness, and culpability shape death verdicts and whether those effects require stronger selection and voir dire protections.

themes.name: Is excluding prospective jurors who oppose the death penalty constitutionally justified?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether death qualification produces a sufficiently competent and impartial capital jury or instead distorts jury representativeness and deliberation.

themes.name: Does the quality of capital defense representation determine whether defendants receive death or life imprisonment?
themes.definition: This question investigates how counsel’s competence, resources, investigation, mitigation presentation, and ethical choices affect capital-sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: Can appellate and post-conviction review correct the systemic errors that produce unjust death sentences?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether review mechanisms identify and remedy unreliable convictions, deficient representation, procedural violations, and disproportionate sentences before execution.

themes.name: Does the gap between formal capital-sentencing law and its practical administration undermine constitutional legitimacy?
themes.definition: This question compares statutory and doctrinal protections with how prosecutors, trial courts, juries, appellate courts, and prison officials actually administer capital punishment.

themes.name: Does comparative proportionality review meaningfully constrain arbitrary death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether state appellate comparisons with other capital cases effectively identify disproportionate sentences or function as a weak and largely symbolic safeguard.

themes.name: Should categorical constitutional rules exclude defendants whose culpability or future development is substantially limited or uncertain?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether reduced mental capacity, youth or developmental immaturity, and comparable vulnerabilities make execution categorically impermissible rather than merely mitigating.

themes.name: Does the risk of wrongful conviction or execution independently undermine the legitimacy of the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question asks whether human fallibility and the possibility of irreversible error make capital punishment unacceptable even when some individual death sentences are legally valid.

themes.name: Are statistical studies of racial discrimination and arbitrariness methodologically strong enough to support constitutional regulation of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the validity, interpretation, and legal significance of empirical evidence used to demonstrate racial disparities or unreliable sentencing patterns.

themes.name: Has Supreme Court constitutional doctrine made capital punishment rational and reliable, or has it preserved a fundamentally defective system?
themes.definition: This question assesses the Supreme Court’s evolving oversight of capital punishment, including its procedural rules, substantive limits, and response to empirical evidence.

themes.name: Can incremental constitutional and institutional reforms meaningfully improve capital punishment without preserving its underlying defects?
themes.definition: This question compares reform strategies—such as narrowing eligibility, improving defense, and strengthening review—with arguments that systemic problems require abolition.

themes.name: Does the inherent cruelty and human suffering of death sentences and executions defeat their moral or constitutional justification?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the harms imposed on condemned prisoners and their broader social consequences are compatible with the state’s claimed purposes for capital punishment.

themes.name: Can the death penalty be justified by deterrence or other social benefits despite its individual and systemic costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether execution frequency, institutional practices, and claimed penological benefits provide sufficient justification for imposing the ultimate punishment.

themes.name: How should responsibility for unjust capital punishment be allocated among prosecutors, judges, jurors, defense lawyers, appellate courts, and corrections officials?
themes.definition: This question investigates how responsibility is distributed or obscured across the institutions and professionals whose cumulative decisions produce death sentences and executions.

themes.name: Have guided-discretion reforms actually eliminated arbitrary death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether statutory aggravating factors, sentencing procedures, and other post-Furman reforms reliably reduce inconsistency, bias, and capriciousness in capital punishment.

themes.name: Can individualized capital sentencing be reconciled with consistency and equal justice?
themes.definition: This question analyzes whether allowing decisionmakers to consider each offender’s circumstances produces fairer outcomes or instead creates unacceptable disparities among formally similar cases.

themes.name: How do capital jurors’ beliefs, emotions, and stereotypes shape life-versus-death decisions?
themes.definition: This question investigates how jurors’ death-penalty attitudes, commonsense assumptions, emotional reactions, and social stereotypes influence capital sentencing.

themes.name: Is jury decision-making sufficiently reasoned and reliable to justify death sentences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether juries can lawfully and consistently perform the moral and factual judgments required when choosing death over a lesser punishment.

themes.name: Does mitigation evidence meaningfully reduce death sentences?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether defendants’ life histories, humanizing evidence, contextual circumstances, and other mitigating information effectively influence culpability assessments and produce life sentences.

themes.name: How should aggravating circumstances and future dangerousness be evaluated at the penalty phase?
themes.definition: This question examines whether aggravating evidence and predictions of future dangerousness are sufficiently accurate, relevant, and constrained to justify capital punishment.

themes.name: Do racial, cultural, and religious identities produce unequal capital-sentencing outcomes?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether defendant identity, racial stereotypes, cultural assumptions, or religious affiliation affect death-sentence decisions and the legitimacy of capital punishment.

themes.name: How do victim characteristics and victim race influence who receives a death sentence?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the social identity and perceived worth of victims, including racial disparities and victim-family participation, affect prosecutorial and sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: Can capital punishment reliably avoid wrongful convictions and irreversible sentencing error?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether capital trials and sentencing systems provide adequate protection against factual innocence, unreliable evidence, and other errors that cannot be remedied after execution.

themes.name: Are capital defense counsel and mitigation teams adequately competent, independent, and resourced?
themes.definition: This question examines whether indigent capital defendants receive effective representation, specialized mitigation investigation, and counsel sufficiently independent from political or judicial pressures.

themes.name: Do prosecutorial, judicial, and local institutional incentives make capital punishment arbitrary?
themes.definition: This question investigates how decentralized discretion, professional incentives, political pressures, and locally constituted legal institutions shape unequal capital-sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: Are postconviction review and procedural remedies adequate to correct capital-case errors?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether state and federal review meaningfully identify and remedy constitutional, evidentiary, and representation failures after a death sentence is imposed.

themes.name: Should constitutional law categorically exclude certain mentally impaired or otherwise less culpable defendants from execution?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the Eighth Amendment permits or requires categorical exemptions based on psychological impairment, mental illness, or diminished culpability.

themes.name: Do execution methods impose unconstitutional risks of cruelty despite efforts to make executions humane?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether execution procedures are sufficiently reliable and painless, or whether their physical and institutional conditions violate the prohibition on cruel and unusual punishment.

themes.name: Can constitutional procedural safeguards make capital sentencing fair and reliable without abolishing it?
themes.definition: This question tests whether additional requirements governing eligibility, trial, sentencing, and review can adequately address systemic arbitrariness while retaining the death penalty.

themes.name: Has Supreme Court regulation under Furman and Gregg provided a coherent constitutional framework for capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question analyzes whether Supreme Court doctrine consistently defines eligibility, discretion, procedural safeguards, and remedies, or leaves major tensions and gaps.

themes.name: Does variation across states, regions, and counties undermine the constitutional legitimacy of the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question examines whether geographic differences in charging, sentencing, and execution practices reflect impermissible arbitrariness rather than legally relevant differences.

themes.name: Can empirical evidence establish that capital punishment is racially biased or systemically unreliable?
themes.definition: This question assesses how statistical and social-scientific research should be used to identify structural disparities and determine their legal significance in capital cases.

themes.name: Can deterrence or other consequentialist benefits justify retaining capital punishment despite its risks?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether claimed crime-control benefits are sufficiently credible and important to outweigh concerns about wrongful execution, arbitrariness, and unequal administration.

themes.name: Can life without parole serve as a legitimate substitute for the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question compares life without parole with execution as a response to the most serious crimes, including their effects on deterrence, retribution, proportionality, and institutional legitimacy.

themes.name: Can state-imposed death be morally and legally justified beyond retribution?
themes.definition: This question examines whether deterrence, incapacitation, desert, or other asserted benefits can justify the state’s uniquely severe and irreversible punishment.

themes.name: Is the American death-penalty system unconstitutional under the Eighth Amendment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether capital punishment as currently authorized and administered violates constitutional prohibitions on cruel, excessive, or degrading punishment.

themes.name: Does the death penalty’s use of execution methods constitute cruel or inhuman punishment?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether particular methods or practices of execution inflict constitutionally impermissible pain, indignity, or psychological harm.

themes.name: Do guided-discretion rules actually prevent arbitrary and inconsistent capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question tests whether statutory aggravators, sentencing instructions, and other formal constraints meaningfully reduce unpredictability in who receives death.

themes.name: Does official discretion permit extralegal factors to determine who is charged, sentenced, or executed?
themes.definition: This question investigates how prosecutors, judges, juries, and other officials use discretionary power in ways that may produce biased or inconsistent capital outcomes.

themes.name: Do racial disparities and racial history render capital punishment constitutionally illegitimate?
themes.definition: This question asks whether persistent racial patterns in capital charging, sentencing, or execution support constitutional challenges to the death-penalty system.

themes.name: How do race, socioeconomic status, and geography shape capital-case outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether defendant race, victim race, poverty, location, or regional variation influences prosecution, sentencing, or execution independently of legally relevant facts.

themes.name: Can capital juries make individualized and reliable life-or-death decisions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether jurors can fairly weigh aggravating and mitigating evidence rather than relying on stereotypes, emotional reactions, or inaccurate perceptions.

themes.name: How do juror emotion, empathy, and culturally situated judgment affect capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question investigates how remorse, perceived dangerousness, racial attitudes, community norms, and other psychological or cultural judgments influence death verdicts.

themes.name: Is mitigation evidence legally and practically effective in preventing death sentences?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether evidence about a defendant’s social history, vulnerability, mental condition, or life circumstances meaningfully changes capital-sentencing decisions.

themes.name: What professional duties must capital defense lawyers meet to make sentencing reliable?
themes.definition: This question examines whether counsel must conduct particular investigations, develop mitigation, consult experts, or otherwise act beyond ordinary professional discretion.

themes.name: When may a defendant’s cognitive or developmental characteristics make execution impermissible?
themes.definition: This question concerns categorical or individualized constitutional limits on executing people whose intellectual, developmental, or other diminished capacities reduce culpability.

themes.name: How should proportionality and evolving standards of decency limit capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the severity of death is proportionate to an offender’s culpability and whether changing national consensus restricts its use.

themes.name: Do capital-case procedural safeguards adequately protect reliability and due process?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether heightened procedures at trial, sentencing, and review sufficiently prevent wrongful, arbitrary, or constitutionally defective death sentences.

themes.name: Should judges or juries possess final authority over capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question examines how allocating sentencing power between juries and judges affects constitutional validity, democratic legitimacy, and the risk of arbitrary outcomes.

themes.name: Does appellate and habeas review effectively detect and remedy defective death sentences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether post-conviction courts obtain adequate factual records and meaningfully correct errors, inadequate representation, or unreliable sentencing decisions.

themes.name: How have Furman, Gregg, and subsequent Supreme Court decisions shaped capital-sentencing regulation?
