themes.definition: This question considers whether the irreversibility and severity of execution justify heightened evidentiary, investigative, review, and error-prevention requirements.

themes.name: Does prosecutorial charging discretion produce arbitrary or racially unequal death-penalty outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines how prosecutors’ decisions about seeking death, selecting charges, and negotiating pleas shape disparities in capital punishment.

themes.name: Are death sentences proportionate to offenders’ culpability and the gravity of their crimes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether capital punishment is reserved for defendants whose responsibility and offense severity distinguish them from similarly situated offenders.

themes.name: Should proportionality review compare capital cases across jurisdictions and offense categories?
themes.definition: This question asks how courts should define the pool of comparable cases when determining whether a death sentence is excessive, inconsistent, or arbitrary.

themes.name: Do empirical studies support the constitutional and policy claims made about capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether quantitative and real-case evidence reliably measures arbitrariness, error, racial disparity, deterrence, and the effects of procedural reforms.

themes.name: Does the death penalty deter murder more effectively than life imprisonment?
themes.definition: This question tests whether the threat or use of execution produces a measurable reduction in homicide beyond the incapacitating effect of noncapital punishment.

themes.name: Do documented errors and systemic defects make abolition preferable to reforming capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question compares the case for eliminating the death penalty with the claim that procedural, institutional, or professional reforms can make it fair and reliable.

themes.name: Do political pressure and public opinion distort the administration and legitimacy of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether elections, punitive political movements, media culture, and changing public support influence death-penalty charging, sentencing, and legal doctrine.

themes.name: Does prolonged death-row incarceration constitute an independently unjust or unconstitutional punishment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether lengthy confinement before execution undermines proportionality, deterrence, dignity, or the constitutional permissibility of the death penalty.

themes.name: Have post-Furman and post-Gregg reforms actually eliminated arbitrariness in capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether guided-discretion statutes, aggravating-factor requirements, and related procedural reforms have made death sentencing consistent, principled, and constitutionally reliable.

themes.name: Does prosecutorial and judicial discretion produce geographically unequal death-penalty outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether local officials, institutional practices, and political incentives cause comparable death-eligible cases to receive different outcomes across counties or states.

themes.name: Does race influence which death-eligible homicide cases result in death sentences?
themes.definition: This question tests whether the race of defendants, victims, or communities affects capital charging, sentencing, or jury decisions after controlling for legally relevant case characteristics.

themes.name: Can systemic racial disparities invalidate a death sentence without proof of case-specific discriminatory intent?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether statistical and historical evidence of structural racial bias should provide a constitutional or legal remedy even when intentional discrimination cannot be shown in an individual case.

themes.name: Do aggravating-factor requirements genuinely restrict death eligibility to the worst murders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether statutory aggravators meaningfully narrow the class of death-eligible defendants rather than merely relabeling a broad range of serious murders.

themes.name: Does capital sentencing adequately distinguish defendants by culpability and moral responsibility?
themes.definition: This question asks whether death sentences are reserved for offenders whose individual responsibility and blameworthiness justify execution rather than life imprisonment.

themes.name: Should diminished culpability or severe mental impairment categorically bar execution?
themes.definition: This question considers whether youth, intellectual disability, mental illness, trauma, or comparable impairments should exclude defendants from execution rather than operate only as mitigating evidence.

themes.name: Does individualized mitigating evidence reliably influence juries toward life sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether defendants’ life histories, trauma, social context, and other mitigating evidence are effectively presented and meaningfully incorporated into death-versus-life decisions.

themes.name: Can capital juries make reliable and lawful individualized death decisions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether jurors can translate legal standards and moral judgments into consistent sentencing outcomes in the penalty phase.

themes.name: Do juror attitudes and biases require stronger selection, voir dire, or instructional safeguards?
themes.definition: This question asks whether opposition to or support for the death penalty, racial attitudes, emotional reactions, and other juror characteristics distort capital sentencing enough to require enhanced procedural protections.

themes.name: Do jury instructions adequately guide death-penalty deliberations?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether instructions sufficiently explain aggravation, mitigation, weighing, mercy, and individualized culpability to prevent arbitrary or legally impermissible sentencing.

themes.name: Can formal legal rules constrain subjective moral and emotional judgments in capital cases?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether doctrinal standards meaningfully control the influence of identity, cultural assumptions, emotion, and nonlegal moral judgments on capital decision-making.

themes.name: Does the death penalty system provide adequate safeguards against wrongful or unreliable convictions and sentences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether trial procedures, evidence standards, defense resources, and institutional checks sufficiently reduce the risk of erroneous death sentences or executions.

themes.name: Does inadequate capital defense representation undermine the reliability of death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether insufficiently qualified counsel, limited resources, or ordinary models of individual-lawyer representation prevent effective investigation, mitigation, and litigation in capital cases.

themes.name: Can appellate and post-conviction review correct constitutional and factual errors in capital cases?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether judicial review, habeas litigation, and post-conviction advocacy meaningfully detect and remedy unreliable or unconstitutional death sentences.

themes.name: Do procedural limits on post-conviction review obstruct meaningful redress for condemned defendants?
themes.definition: This question asks whether filing deadlines, deference rules, procedural default, and other barriers prevent courts from reaching the merits of serious capital-case claims.

themes.name: Does death-row confinement impose unjustified psychological suffering beyond the punishment of execution?
themes.definition: This question examines whether prolonged isolation, uncertainty, and psychiatric distress on death row constitute gratuitous or constitutionally relevant additional punishment.

themes.name: Is it legally and morally permissible for death-row prisoners to waive appeals and hasten execution?
themes.definition: This question considers whether prisoners possess meaningful autonomy to forgo review and whether the state may accept such waivers given coercion, mental illness, and the risk of wrongful execution.

themes.name: Can empirical and social-science evidence establish whether capital punishment is fair and reliable?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how statistical, historical, psychological, and professional evidence should be used by courts and policymakers to assess racial bias, arbitrariness, culpability, and execution reliability.

themes.name: Does the Eighth Amendment constitutionally permit the modern administration of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether contemporary death-penalty practices satisfy evolving standards of decency, national-consensus principles, and the constitutional requirements of proportionality and nonarbitrariness.

themes.name: Can incremental legal reforms resolve the death penalty’s legitimacy problems, or is abolition required?
themes.definition: This question weighs whether procedural restrictions and targeted reforms can make state execution morally and legally acceptable or whether the system’s defects require abolition.

themes.name: Have post-Furman and post-Gregg reforms eliminated arbitrariness in capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question examines whether modern statutory, procedural, and constitutional reforms have made death sentences consistently tied to legally relevant culpability rather than discretionary or unpredictable factors.

themes.name: How does prosecutorial discretion determine which death-eligible defendants actually receive death sentences?
themes.definition: This question investigates how prosecutors select, pursue, or decline capital charges and whether those choices produce unequal outcomes among similarly situated defendants.

themes.name: Does decentralized, county-level administration make capital punishment geographically arbitrary?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether jurisdictional variation in charging practices, resources, legal rules, and local preferences causes comparable cases to receive different capital outcomes.

themes.name: Does jury discretion produce arbitrary or racially disparate death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines how jurors’ discretion, beliefs, emotions, and assessments of culpability shape life-or-death decisions beyond formally defined aggravating and mitigating factors.

themes.name: How do racial perceptions of defendants and victims affect capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether racial composition, stereotypes, or racially differentiated evaluations of character and mitigation influence death-sentence decisions.

themes.name: Can individualized consideration of mitigation be reconciled with consistent and non-arbitrary capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether courts and juries can account for each defendant’s circumstances while maintaining objective constraints on the imposition of death.

themes.name: How should mental illness, intellectual disability, youth, and severe social deprivation affect capital eligibility?
themes.definition: This question examines whether and why diminished maturity, psychological impairment, intellectual disability, or deprived life circumstances reduce culpability or constitutionally bar execution.

themes.name: Does the quality of capital defense counsel determine whether defendants receive death sentences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how attorney competence, experience, resources, investigation, mitigation development, and humanizing representation affect capital-case outcomes.

themes.name: What evidence should be admitted and given weight during the capital sentencing phase?
themes.definition: This question examines the legal and practical treatment of mitigating, exculpatory, psychological, psychiatric, character, and future-dangerousness evidence in death-sentence decisions.

themes.name: Do capital-sentencing rules adequately narrow death eligibility to the most culpable offenders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether statutory aggravators, proportionality rules, and Eighth Amendment doctrine meaningfully distinguish defendants deserving death from those who should receive a lesser punishment.

themes.name: Are heightened procedural safeguards constitutionally necessary because death is qualitatively different from other punishments?
themes.definition: This question asks whether the irreversible and severe nature of execution requires stronger protections against error, prejudice, and arbitrary decision-making than ordinary sentencing.

themes.name: Do appellate and habeas review mechanisms meaningfully correct capital-sentencing and conviction errors?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether judicial review, post-conviction procedures, and procedural avenues for challenging death sentences reliably detect and remedy constitutional violations and factual mistakes.

themes.name: How serious is the risk of wrongful conviction or execution within the capital-punishment system?
themes.definition: This question investigates the sources, frequency, and constitutional significance of mistaken convictions, erroneous death sentences, and executions of potentially innocent defendants.

themes.name: Do execution methods and post-sentencing procedures create unconstitutional risks of cruel and unusual punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the methods and administration of execution expose condemned people to excessive pain, psychological suffering, delay, or degrading treatment.

themes.name: Can deterrence, incapacitation, or retribution provide a valid justification for retaining the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether capital punishment produces distinctive crime-control benefits or satisfies a defensible retributive principle that lesser punishments cannot provide.

themes.name: Is state-imposed execution morally and constitutionally legitimate?
themes.definition: This question examines the state’s authority and responsibility to impose death, including whether legal institutions can legitimately authorize and participate in an irreversible punishment.

themes.name: Does empirical evidence of unequal outcomes undermine the constitutional validity of formally neutral capital rules?
themes.definition: This question analyzes the tension between facially constitutional procedures and observed disparities, implementation failures, and extralegal influences in actual capital cases.

themes.name: Is Supreme Court capital-punishment jurisprudence coherent and effective in limiting state discretion?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the consistency, predictability, and practical force of Supreme Court doctrine governing eligibility, sentencing procedures, review, and constitutional safeguards.

themes.name: Does prolonged capital litigation improve fairness or produce an expensive and dysfunctional system?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether extended appeals and post-conviction proceedings meaningfully enhance reliability and justice or instead create systemic delay, cost, and institutional dysfunction.

themes.name: Are declining death sentences and public support signaling the institutional abandonment of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether reduced executions, fewer death verdicts, life-without-parole alternatives, and changing political and social attitudes indicate a durable shift away from the death penalty.

themes.name: Do post-Furman and post-Gregg procedural safeguards actually prevent arbitrary and inconsistent death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether statutory guidance, bifurcated trials, appellate review, and other constitutional reforms have produced reliable and nonarbitrary capital sentencing in practice.

themes.name: Do aggravating-factor requirements meaningfully narrow death eligibility to the most culpable offenders?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether statutory aggravators genuinely distinguish death-worthy cases or merely provide an appearance of constraint while leaving substantial discretion.

themes.name: Can individualized mitigation be reconciled with consistent and nonarbitrary capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question investigates how courts and juries should weigh personal history, mental condition, and contextual explanations without producing unpredictable outcomes.

themes.name: How do racial and demographic biases shape capital charging, sentencing, and execution decisions?
themes.definition: This question studies whether race, victim characteristics, defendant identity, or historically racialized institutions produce unequal outcomes throughout the death-penalty process.

themes.name: Does the death penalty system adequately protect against wrongful convictions and erroneous executions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether investigative, trial, evidentiary, and review procedures reliably identify factual and legal errors before an irreversible execution occurs.

themes.name: Does inadequate defense representation make capital sentencing constitutionally unreliable?
themes.definition: This question examines whether limited resources, deficient investigation, weak mitigation development, or the distinctive demands of capital defense systematically distort life-or-death decisions.

themes.name: What ethical and constitutional limits govern defense counsel when a capital defendant’s wishes conflict with counsel’s judgment?
themes.definition: This question concerns counsel’s obligations when defendants resist mitigation, seek execution, waive appeals, or otherwise exercise autonomy in ways that may threaten reliable representation.

themes.name: Are death-qualified juries sufficiently impartial and constitutionally representative?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether excluding prospective jurors opposed to capital punishment protects the state’s interests at the cost of reducing jury impartiality, diversity, or attention to mitigation.

themes.name: How do capital-jury procedures affect jurors’ willingness and ability to consider life rather than death?
themes.definition: This question investigates how jury instructions, deliberation structures, emotional evidence, and decision rules influence sentencing judgments and the consideration of mitigating circumstances.

themes.name: Should mental disability or impaired cognitive functioning bar execution or reduce culpability?
themes.definition: This question examines how constitutional doctrine and legal classifications should identify defendants whose intellectual, psychological, or cognitive condition makes execution impermissible or less justified.

themes.name: How should legal factfinders use psychological and clinical evidence in capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the reliability and proper role of expert evidence about mental illness, cognitive functioning, future dangerousness, and responsibility in death-penalty decisions.

themes.name: Does prolonged death-row incarceration constitute cruel, excessive, or otherwise unjustified punishment?
themes.definition: This question considers whether extended confinement under the threat of execution creates an independently unconstitutional or morally unacceptable punishment.

themes.name: Are mandatory or defendant-requested death sentences compatible with individualized capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question asks whether the state may impose or carry out death without ordinary individualized sentencing, particularly when a defendant waives mitigation or seeks execution.

themes.name: How does Supreme Court doctrine shape the constitutional boundaries and practical variation of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question studies whether the Court’s methods, changing standards, and review practices meaningfully constrain state systems or generate doctrinal uncertainty and unequal outcomes.

themes.name: Can judicial review and post-conviction relief correct constitutional defects before execution?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the availability, timing, and effectiveness of appellate and collateral remedies for flawed trials, unreliable evidence, inadequate counsel, or unlawful sentencing.

themes.name: How do prosecutors, judges, juries, and local institutions distribute discretionary death-penalty outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines how institutional capacity, political pressures, regional practices, and actor-specific choices create variation in capital charging and sentencing.

themes.name: Does empirical evidence support the deterrent or other consequentialist justifications for capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether research shows that executions produce crime-control or broader criminal-justice benefits sufficient to support their use.

themes.name: Is state-imposed execution morally and legally justified despite its risks of error and unequal application?
themes.definition: This question weighs retributive, deterrent, incapacitative, and expressive justifications against the human, legal, and institutional harms of execution.

themes.name: Can incremental reform make the modern death-penalty system legitimate, or does persistent defect require abolition?
themes.definition: This question compares pragmatic reforms with abolition by asking whether recurring arbitrariness, discrimination, error, and institutional failure are remediable within a death-penalty regime.

themes.name: How do narratives about defendants, victims, and state violence shape judgments of capital culpability?
themes.definition: This question investigates how legal storytelling, mitigation narratives, journalism, and representations of crime influence perceptions of responsibility, humanity, punishment, and legitimacy.

themes.name: Have post-Furman and post-Gregg reforms actually eliminated arbitrary death-sentence selection?
themes.definition: This question examines whether guided-discretion statutes, jury instructions, and related reforms have meaningfully reduced inconsistent or capricious capital sentencing.

themes.name: Do statutory eligibility and aggravating factors restrict execution to the most culpable offenders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether death-penalty eligibility rules narrow punishment to defendants whose conduct and blameworthiness justify execution.

themes.name: Does individualized consideration of mitigation prevent capital sentencing from becoming an offense-centered decision?
themes.definition: This question asks whether courts and juries adequately consider a defendant’s character, background, mental condition, and life circumstances rather than focusing only on the crime.

themes.name: Do capital juries genuinely weigh aggravating and mitigating evidence when choosing between life and death?
themes.definition: This question investigates how jurors interpret instructions, assess competing evidence, and exercise discretion in life-or-death sentencing decisions.

themes.name: Does the quality of capital defense representation affect whether defendants receive death rather than life imprisonment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether counsel competence, investigation, funding, specialized preparation, and advocacy materially influence capital sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: Can heightened procedural safeguards reliably prevent wrongful convictions and executions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether enhanced standards for capital trials, review, and execution adequately address factual uncertainty and the risk of punishing innocent people.

themes.name: Does racial bias, especially in cases involving Black defendants and white victims, influence death-sentence selection?
themes.definition: This question tests whether race, racialized social narratives, or unconscious bias affects eligibility, sentencing, or perceptions of culpability in capital cases.

themes.name: Are mentally impaired defendants adequately protected from capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question assesses the legal standards and evidence used to identify intellectual disability, mental impairment, or diminished capacity as grounds for exemption or mitigation.

themes.name: Are psychiatric and medical experts reliable and appropriately limited in capital litigation?
themes.definition: This question examines the validity, scope, and courtroom use of forensic mental-health assessments concerning competence, culpability, dangerousness, and execution eligibility.

themes.name: Is imposing the death penalty on youthful defendants constitutionally and proportionally permissible?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether juveniles’ developmental immaturity and reduced culpability require categorical or individualized limits on capital punishment.

themes.name: How should empirical evidence influence constitutional review of capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question asks whether data on arbitrariness, racial disparities, reliability, and institutional performance should shape judicial evaluations of death-penalty schemes.

themes.name: Do Supreme Court death-penalty standards meaningfully constrain state trial and sentencing practices?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether evolving Eighth Amendment doctrine is consistently implemented by state courts, trial judges, and sentencing authorities.

themes.name: Do appellate and habeas procedures provide an effective remedy for constitutional errors in capital cases?
themes.definition: This question examines whether procedural rules, deference, and barriers to review prevent courts from correcting unreliable or unjust death sentences.

themes.name: Do political and institutional incentives undermine the fair administration of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how prosecutors, legislators, judges, law-enforcement officials, and other institutional actors may encourage excessive, inconsistent, or biased capital sentencing.

themes.name: Why does formal authorization of the death penalty produce rare and geographically uneven executions?
themes.definition: This question examines the gap between statutes authorizing capital punishment and its actual use across jurisdictions, including variation among states such as Illinois, California, and Texas.

themes.name: Do portrayals of victims, defendants, and crime participants distort capital sentencing beyond legally relevant culpability?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether narratives about victim worth, defendant character, threat, or crime seriousness improperly influence life-or-death judgments.

themes.name: Are execution methods consistent with the constitutional requirement that punishment not be cruel or inhumane?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the design and administration of execution methods provide a sufficiently reliable and humane means of carrying out death sentences.

themes.name: Does the availability of life imprisonment without parole alter the justification and use of the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question examines whether life without parole functions as an adequate alternative to execution and changes arguments about necessity, proportionality, or sentencing choice.

themes.name: Should capital punishment be abolished rather than made constitutional through further procedural regulation?
themes.definition: This question compares abolition with incremental legal and policy reform as responses to persistent arbitrariness, inequality, error, and institutional dysfunction.

themes.name: Can community moral judgment legitimately determine who deserves execution?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether jury and community participation supplies democratic and retributive legitimacy or instead introduces subjective and socially unequal judgments into capital sentencing.

themes.name: Do constitutionally approved capital-sentencing procedures actually prevent arbitrary and unreliable death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether formal safeguards, legal standards, and judicial review meaningfully constrain arbitrary decision-making in practice.

themes.name: Do capital-sentencing rules genuinely reserve execution for the most culpable offenders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether statutory eligibility rules and case-selection practices adequately narrow the death penalty to unusually blameworthy defendants.

themes.name: How do the race of defendants and victims affect capital-sentencing and execution outcomes?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether racial disparities or discrimination influence charging, sentencing, jury decisions, or execution across defendant- and victim-race combinations.

themes.name: Do socioeconomic and other forms of marginalization produce unequal access to capital justice?
themes.definition: This question examines whether poverty, social marginalization, or culturally disfavored status affects death-penalty selection, defense quality, or sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: How frequently do capital-case errors produce wrongful convictions or undeserved death sentences?
themes.definition: This question assesses the incidence, sources, and consequences of factual and procedural error in capital prosecutions.

themes.name: Does inadequate capital defense representation undermine the reliability of death sentences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether insufficient funding, investigation, mitigation development, or attorney performance causes unreliable capital convictions or sentences.

themes.name: How do capital juries’ deliberations and perceptions shape life-or-death sentencing decisions?
themes.definition: This question studies how juror attitudes, interpersonal pressure, emotional responses, and treatment of mitigation influence capital verdicts.

themes.name: Does prosecutorial discretion make capital-case selection arbitrary or discriminatory?
themes.definition: This question examines whether prosecutors’ charging and case-selection choices create death-penalty disparities unrelated to legally relevant culpability.

themes.name: Does the weighing of aggravating and mitigating evidence produce proportionate capital sentences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether decision makers consistently and constitutionally balance offense severity against mitigating facts about the defendant.

themes.name: Should individualized judgment prevail over categorical labels in determining deathworthiness?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether capital decisions should depend primarily on defendant-specific facts rather than generalized classifications of offenders or offenses.

themes.name: How should intellectual disability be defined and established in death-penalty proceedings?
themes.definition: This question examines the legal standards, evidentiary requirements, and institutional practices used to determine whether intellectual disability bars execution.

themes.name: Should defendants with reduced culpability or non-killing involvement be categorically exempt from execution?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the constitutional and moral limits of imposing death on accomplices, non-killers, or offenders whose culpability is substantially diminished.

themes.name: Does prolonged delay in capital cases create an independent injustice or constitutional problem?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether systemic delays in adjudication, review, or execution themselves undermine fairness, legality, or the legitimacy of punishment.

themes.name: Are postconviction review and collateral remedies adequate to correct capital-case errors?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether existing review mechanisms can effectively identify and remedy ineffective assistance, unreliable evidence, and other capital-defense failures.

themes.name: Should empirical evidence about capital punishment influence constitutional judgments?
themes.definition: This question considers whether statistical, behavioral, and social-science evidence should shape courts’ evaluation of the death penalty’s fairness, reliability, and constitutionality.

themes.name: Does variation among states and local jurisdictions make capital punishment unconstitutionally arbitrary?
themes.definition: This question examines whether geographically uneven statutes, charging practices, jury outcomes, and execution patterns produce punishment differences unrelated to culpability.

themes.name: Do the actual conditions and methods of execution undermine the legitimacy of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether botched, painful, or degrading executions create independent constitutional, moral, or institutional objections to the death penalty.

themes.name: Can institutional and judicial reform make capital punishment legitimate, or do its systemic defects require abolition?
themes.definition: This question tests whether procedural and institutional reforms can cure persistent failures in capital punishment or whether those failures are irreparable.

themes.name: How does Eighth Amendment doctrine define and revise the constitutional limits of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines how evolving standards of decency, proportionality, and judicial interpretation constrain eligibility, sentencing procedures, and execution.

themes.name: Do capital-case institutions adequately protect defendant autonomy and personhood against state-inflicted death?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether lawyers, courts, juries, and evidentiary practices preserve individualized human consideration rather than reducing defendants to legal or emotional abstractions.

themes.name: Do post-Furman guided-discretion procedures actually prevent arbitrary and capricious death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether statutory aggravating factors, sentencing instructions, and other formal constraints meaningfully reduce arbitrariness in capital sentencing.

themes.name: How much does prosecutorial discretion determine whether a defendant receives death or life imprisonment?
themes.definition: This question investigates how charging decisions, plea negotiations, advocacy resources, and local prosecutorial practices shape capital outcomes.

themes.name: Do geographic and state-level differences produce unjustified disparities in capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether county, state, or regional variation in capital charging and sentencing reflects legally irrelevant institutional or social conditions.

themes.name: Is capital punishment applied in a racially discriminatory manner?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether race affects capital charging, sentencing, or execution outcomes after accounting for legally relevant features of the offense and defendant.

themes.name: How do capital jurors actually make life-or-death decisions, and what forms of bias distort those decisions?
themes.definition: This question compares jurors’ empirical decision-making processes with formal legal models, focusing on attitudes, representativeness, mitigation, and racial or other biases.

themes.name: Does individualized consideration and mitigation evidence meaningfully prevent death sentences based solely on the offense?
themes.definition: This question examines whether capital sentencing gives adequate weight to a defendant’s background, character, mental condition, and other mitigating circumstances.

themes.name: Does capital sentencing reserve death for defendants who are sufficiently culpable and deathworthy?
themes.definition: This question asks whether constitutional and institutional rules distinguish appropriately among offenders based on moral responsibility, participation, intent, and the seriousness of the crime.

themes.name: How should intellectual disability and other cognitive limitations restrict eligibility for execution?
themes.definition: This question studies the constitutional and moral treatment of defendants whose mental or cognitive capacities may undermine culpability or the legitimacy of execution.

themes.name: Do capital adjudication systems create an unacceptable risk of wrongful convictions, death sentences, or executions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the prevalence and systemic sources of factual error, unreliable evidence, mistaken judgments, and irreversible wrongful punishment in capital cases.

themes.name: Does inadequate funding or representation make capital defense constitutionally and practically unreliable?
themes.definition: This question examines whether insufficiently qualified, resourced, or independent defense counsel fail to investigate, present mitigation, or challenge the prosecution effectively.

themes.name: How do penalty-phase evidentiary rules shape the reliability and fairness of capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether expert testimony, contested factual evidence, and procedural limits on mitigation help or hinder accurate life-or-death decisions.

themes.name: Can appellate and post-conviction review reliably correct erroneous or arbitrary death sentences?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether courts, procedural avenues, and standards of review effectively identify and remedy constitutional, factual, and institutional failures after conviction.

themes.name: Does Supreme Court death-penalty doctrine adequately respond to empirical evidence of arbitrariness and unreliability?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether Eighth Amendment doctrine, evolving standards, and judicial review reflect what research shows about actual capital-sentencing practices.

themes.name: Why do state capital-punishment reforms often fail to change actual criminal-justice practice?
themes.definition: This question examines the gap between formal statutory or constitutional reforms and their implementation by prosecutors, courts, juries, and other institutions.

themes.name: What empirical methods can validly establish whether capital punishment is fair and racially neutral?
themes.definition: This question concerns the adequacy of aggregate rates, longitudinal comparisons, case matching, and other empirical strategies for evaluating capital-punishment disparities.

themes.name: Can capital punishment be reconciled with retributive justice, mercy, and humane limits on state violence?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the desire to condemn and proportionately punish serious wrongdoing justifies execution despite moral limits concerning compassion, dignity, and irreversible harm.

themes.name: How do political pressure, public sentiment, media narratives, and social perceptions influence capital outcomes?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether condemnation, advocacy, victim-related interests, public understanding, and characterizations of defendants affect decisions beyond legally relevant evidence.

themes.name: Do botched, painful, or otherwise problematic executions undermine the legitimacy of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the manner of execution creates independent constitutional or moral objections to the state’s authority to carry out death sentences.

themes.name: How does the federal death penalty for drug-related killings and drug kingpins operate within ordinary capital-punishment principles?
themes.definition: This question assesses the legal justification, implementation, and distinctive fairness concerns surrounding federal capital prosecutions for drug-related conduct.

themes.name: Can procedural reform make capital punishment sufficiently reliable, or do systemic flaws support abolition?
themes.definition: This question weighs limited institutional reforms against the possibility that persistent arbitrariness, discrimination, error, and state violence make the death penalty fundamentally illegitimate.

themes.name: Can guided-discretion rules prevent arbitrary and inconsistent capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question examines whether statutory aggravating-factor schemes, sentencing standards, and related constraints meaningfully regularize decisions about who receives death.

themes.name: Do capital-eligibility rules exclude defendants whose cases do not warrant execution?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether broad or unclear legal definitions of death-eligible crimes create overinclusive, inconsistent, or constitutionally excessive exposure to the death penalty.

themes.name: Do capital-jury procedures produce reliable and nonarbitrary life-or-death decisions?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether jury selection, deliberation, instructions, and penalty-phase voting adequately protect against confusion, bias, and arbitrary death verdicts.

themes.name: Does assigning sentencing authority to judges rather than juries affect capital-sentencing fairness?
themes.definition: This question compares judicial and jury control over death sentencing and asks whether either institutional arrangement produces more consistent, legitimate, or constitutionally sound outcomes.

themes.name: How does individualized mitigating evidence affect capital sentencing and culpability judgments?
themes.definition: This question examines whether defendants’ character, history, life circumstances, and other mitigating evidence are meaningfully considered when deciding between life and death.

themes.name: Should mental impairment or diminished capacity categorically bar execution?
themes.definition: This question evaluates constitutional and normative limits on executing defendants with intellectual disability, developmental disability, severe mental illness, or impaired decision-making capacity.

themes.name: Does racial bias—especially in cases involving Black defendants and white victims—shape death-sentencing outcomes?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether race affects charging, jury decision-making, sentencing, or execution independently of legally relevant offense and culpability factors.

themes.name: Do local racial demographics influence the likelihood of receiving a death sentence?
themes.definition: This question tests whether county or community composition, including the racial identity of defendants and victims, predicts capital outcomes through local institutional or social mechanisms.

themes.name: Do victim-related, emotional, or other legally irrelevant factors distort capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question asks whether information about victims, families, community sentiment, politics, or other extralegal considerations improperly influences life-or-death decisions.

themes.name: Does the quality and funding of capital defense counsel affect death-sentencing outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether inadequate investigation, weak mitigation presentations, limited resources, or deficient legal representation increase the risk of a death sentence.

themes.name: How reliably do capital proceedings distinguish guilty and highly culpable defendants from those facing serious error?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether trial procedures, evidence evaluation, and sentencing judgments sufficiently reduce wrongful convictions, unreliable death sentences, and unjust executions.

themes.name: Do appellate, habeas, and post-conviction procedures effectively correct unjust capital sentences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether review mechanisms identify and remedy constitutional violations, factual errors, deficient representation, and other defects after conviction and sentencing.

themes.name: Have post-Furman procedural reforms actually reduced arbitrariness in the death penalty’s operation?
themes.definition: This question compares the formal safeguards established after Furman and Gregg with empirical patterns in contemporary capital charging, sentencing, review, and execution.

themes.name: Is proportionality review necessary to prevent excessive or inconsistent capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question considers whether courts must compare a death sentence with the offense, the offender’s culpability, and sentences in similar cases to satisfy constitutional proportionality requirements.

themes.name: Does capital punishment track individualized culpability rather than structural or procedural accident?
themes.definition: This question asks whether execution is reserved for defendants whose personal responsibility and offense circumstances justify death, rather than for those affected by jurisdiction, counsel, or decision-maker variation.

themes.name: Can deterrence justify executing defendants with diminished blameworthiness?
themes.definition: This question tests whether any deterrent benefit can provide a sufficient justification for executing defendants whose mental condition, constrained agency, or other characteristics weaken retributive blameworthiness.

themes.name: Does retribution provide a constitutionally and morally adequate justification for the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether desert-based punishment can legitimately support execution for a narrowly defined class of especially serious murders.

themes.name: Do public opinion and evolving social standards constrain or sustain capital-punishment policy?
themes.definition: This question examines how public attitudes, social conflict, political change, and changing norms affect death-penalty reform and constitutional judgments about its acceptability.

themes.name: Does Supreme Court doctrine meaningfully protect capital defendants from arbitrary or excessive punishment?
themes.definition: This question analyzes whether the Court’s Eighth Amendment jurisprudence establishes clear, enforceable, and practically effective limits on capital sentencing and execution.

themes.name: Can institutional reforms overcome the administrative and resource constraints that undermine capital-case fairness?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether changes to courts, legislatures, legal representation, review systems, and litigation funding can correct systemic defects without relying solely on abolition or moral condemnation.

themes.name: Do post-Furman procedural safeguards actually prevent arbitrary capital sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether guided-discretion rules, statutory safeguards, and related reforms have meaningfully reduced arbitrary or capricious death sentences.

themes.name: Does capital sentencing reliably distinguish the worst offenders from the broader class of murderers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether eligibility rules and sentencing practices consistently restrict death sentences to offenders judged most culpable.

themes.name: How does prosecutorial discretion produce geographic and racial disparities in capital charging and sentencing?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether prosecutors’ decisions about seeking death create unequal enforcement across jurisdictions and defendant or victim groups.

themes.name: Does the race of the murder victim influence capital charges and death sentences?
themes.definition: This question tests whether cases involving white victims receive more severe capital outcomes than otherwise comparable cases involving victims of other races.

themes.name: How do defendant race, socioeconomic status, and social background affect capital punishment outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether characteristics of defendants and their life circumstances influence charging, sentencing, or execution decisions beyond legally relevant factors.

themes.name: How do jury composition and juror attitudes shape capital sentencing decisions?
themes.definition: This question studies whether juror demographics, death-penalty views, biases, and courtroom influences affect the decision to impose death.

themes.name: How do jurors’ emotional responses to defendants and victims affect life-or-death sentencing?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether empathy, perceived remorse, victim sympathy, and emotional narratives systematically influence capital sentencing.

themes.name: Should judges or juries have final authority over capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question compares the fairness, reliability, and constitutional consequences of allocating capital-sentencing power to juries rather than judges.

themes.name: Does individualized mitigation meaningfully constrain or improve capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether consideration of a defendant’s personal history, family circumstances, trauma, and other mitigating evidence produces more accurate and less arbitrary sentences.

themes.name: Should mental illness, intellectual disability, youth, or trauma restrict eligibility for execution?
themes.definition: This question examines whether diminished cognitive or psychological capacity should categorically bar or substantially limit capital punishment.

themes.name: Does defense counsel provide constitutionally adequate and adequately funded representation in capital cases?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether counsel’s competence, resources, investigation, and attorney-client relationship are sufficient to protect defendants facing execution.

themes.name: Does unequal funding of capital defense contribute to wrongful or excessive death sentences?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether resource disparities among defense systems affect investigation, mitigation, litigation quality, and sentencing outcomes.

themes.name: Do discovery and disclosure failures by prosecutors cause unjust capital convictions or sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether withholding exculpatory or mitigating evidence undermines the accuracy and legitimacy of capital adjudication.

themes.name: Can appellate, habeas, and post-conviction review reliably correct capital-case errors?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether institutional review after conviction identifies and remedies constitutional violations, unreliable verdicts, and wrongful death sentences.

themes.name: How do procedural choices in federal and state capital litigation affect access to review and legal remedies?
themes.definition: This question studies how jurisdictional fragmentation, procedural rules, and institutional design determine whether capital defendants can obtain meaningful review.

themes.name: Does fragmented state and local administration produce inconsistent capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether decentralized institutions and local discretion create substantial differences in death-penalty enforcement across jurisdictions.

themes.name: Are capital-sentencing procedures sufficiently reliable given the risk of wrongful conviction and execution?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether the extraordinary possibility of factual or legal error is compatible with imposing an irreversible punishment.

themes.name: Should proof beyond a reasonable doubt be supplemented when jurors retain doubts about guilt in capital cases?
themes.definition: This question considers whether capital sentencing requires additional safeguards when jurors believe guilt is legally established but remain subjectively uncertain.

themes.name: Can constitutional regulation meaningfully constrain capital punishment without categorically abolishing it?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether Eighth Amendment doctrine and Supreme Court review can impose effective limits on death-penalty practices short of a complete ban.

themes.name: Does the irreversible severity of death justify stronger procedural protections than ordinary criminal punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether capital defendants should receive heightened safeguards because execution is uniquely severe, final, and difficult to remedy.

themes.name: Can lethal-injection protocols satisfy constitutional standards for humane execution?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether particular execution methods and drug protocols create impermissible risks of pain, suffering, or arbitrary administration.

themes.name: Is the death penalty morally and constitutionally justified when life imprisonment can protect the public?
themes.definition: This question compares the claimed necessity of execution with the availability of life imprisonment and weighs competing arguments about deterrence, retribution, and public safety.

themes.name: Do empirical failures in death-penalty administration undermine its legal and moral legitimacy?
themes.definition: This question asks whether racial disparities, error, inconsistency, reversals, delay, and institutional dysfunction make continued capital punishment unjustifiable.

themes.name: Have post-Furman capital-sentencing procedures actually eliminated arbitrary and inconsistent death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether guided-discretion rules, aggravating factors, and related reforms have meaningfully reduced unexplained variation in capital outcomes.

themes.name: Can capital-sentencing rules constrain arbitrariness without eliminating individualized consideration of defendants?
themes.definition: This question addresses the constitutional and practical tension between uniform sentencing standards and attention to character, background, culpability, and mitigation.

themes.name: How do jurors’ emotions, compassion, and perceptions of defendant character influence life-or-death sentencing decisions?
themes.definition: This question investigates how emotional reactions, humanizing information, and moral judgments about defendants and victims affect capital-jury outcomes.

themes.name: Does death qualification produce juries that are sufficiently impartial and representative for capital cases?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether excluding jurors who oppose or cannot impose the death penalty undermines impartiality, jury composition, or reliable decision-making.

themes.name: How do capital juries deliberate and allocate responsibility when deciding whether to impose death?
themes.definition: This question examines deliberation, unanimity, responsibility-sharing, and the jury’s role in authorizing or rejecting state-imposed execution.

themes.name: Does race influence which defendants receive death sentences?
themes.definition: This question tests whether defendant race affects charging, sentencing, or other discretionary decisions in capital cases.

themes.name: Does the race or social status of the victim influence the likelihood of a death sentence?
themes.definition: This question examines whether victim characteristics create unequal valuations of victims and racially patterned capital outcomes.

themes.name: How does local community context shape unequal capital-sentencing outcomes?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether county demographics, local political culture, institutional resources, and decentralized decision-making affect death-penalty decisions.

themes.name: How much does prosecutorial discretion determine who is exposed to the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question focuses on prosecutors’ choices about charging, seeking death, negotiating pleas, and selecting cases for capital prosecution.

themes.name: Do capital defense counsel and mitigation specialists provide representation capable of making sentencing reliable and individualized?
themes.definition: This question evaluates defense resources, investigation, mitigation development, and ineffective-assistance standards in capital proceedings.

themes.name: Are formal procedural rights meaningful when capital defendants lack the practical resources needed to use them?
themes.definition: This question examines the gap between formally guaranteed safeguards and their implementation under conditions of poverty, limited counsel, institutional pressure, or unequal resources.

themes.name: Do appellate and habeas courts adequately correct errors and prevent unjust executions?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether post-trial judicial review identifies and remedies constitutional, evidentiary, and representational failures in capital cases.

themes.name: Do state courts and legislatures faithfully implement Supreme Court limits on capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines how federal constitutional rulings are translated into state statutes, procedures, and decisions.

themes.name: How should intellectual disability and other mental impairments affect eligibility for execution?
themes.definition: This question concerns the legal definitions, evidentiary standards, and expert assessments used to determine whether cognitively impaired defendants may be executed.

themes.name: Do juvenile capital-sentencing schemes impose punishment disproportionate to age-related culpability?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether sentencing rules for juvenile offenders produce arbitrary, inconsistent, or constitutionally excessive punishment.

themes.name: Does capital punishment reliably distinguish the most culpable offenders from other serious offenders?
themes.definition: This question tests whether eligibility and proportionality rules limit death sentences to offenders whose culpability constitutionally and morally justifies execution.

themes.name: How serious is the risk of executing innocent people in a procedurally fallible capital system?
themes.definition: This question examines wrongful convictions, unreliable evidence, trial error, and the capacity of capital procedures to detect innocence before execution.

themes.name: Do procedural reforms improve capital punishment or merely preserve a fundamentally defective system?
themes.definition: This question compares the effects and unintended consequences of incremental safeguards with arguments for structural reform or abolition.

themes.name: How do empirical evidence, public opinion, and mediated narratives affect the legitimacy of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question investigates how real-world outcomes, social-science findings, public discourse, and simplified cultural narratives shape acceptance of the death penalty.

themes.name: Is state-imposed execution morally and constitutionally legitimate despite its irreversible consequences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the retributive, moral, constitutional, and institutional justifications for allowing the state to impose irreversible death as punishment.

themes.name: Do contemporary capital-sentencing systems satisfy the Eighth Amendment’s requirement that death not be imposed arbitrarily or capriciously?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether modern statutory rules, judicial review, and institutional practices meaningfully constrain arbitrary and inconsistent death sentences.

themes.name: Do capital-case procedures reliably distinguish defendants who deserve death from those who should receive life imprisonment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether fact-finding, eligibility rules, aggravating factors, and sentencing procedures produce accurate and dependable death-versus-life decisions.

themes.name: Do wrongful convictions, erroneous death sentences, and the risk of wrongful execution undermine the legitimacy of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether the possibility of irreversible error creates a justification for heightened safeguards, moratoria, or abolition.

themes.name: Does post-conviction review adequately detect and remedy constitutional violations in capital cases?
themes.definition: This question examines whether habeas proceedings, appellate review, and evidence outside the trial record provide an effective safeguard against unreliable or unjust death sentences.

themes.name: Do death-qualified juries favor conviction and death sentences in ways that compromise capital defendants’ rights?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether excluding jurors unwilling to impose death produces juries biased toward punitive judgments or less representative decision-making.

themes.name: How do capital jurors use aggravating, mitigating, moral, and factual considerations when deciding whether a defendant should receive death?
themes.definition: This question concerns the empirical processes through which jurors interpret evidence and translate it into life-or-death sentencing decisions.

themes.name: Does racial bias or the race of defendants and victims produce unequal capital-sentencing outcomes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether racial categories influence charging, sentencing, jury judgments, or execution decisions and whether those effects constitute discrimination or arbitrariness.

themes.name: Do geographic and local political differences make capital punishment arbitrarily dependent on jurisdiction?
themes.definition: This question examines whether county, state, or regional variation in prosecution and sentencing produces unequal chances of receiving or ultimately facing execution.

themes.name: Does broad prosecutorial discretion determine who faces the death penalty in ways that are arbitrary, geographically uneven, or racially unequal?
themes.definition: This question focuses on how prosecutors select capital cases and whether charging discretion escapes meaningful legal or institutional constraint.

themes.name: Do inadequate defense representation and failures to investigate mitigation undermine the reliability of death sentences?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether incompetent counsel, insufficient investigation, or incomplete mitigation presentation causes defendants to receive death when a fair process would not.

themes.name: Should capital sentencing require individualized consideration of aggravating and mitigating evidence despite pressures for structured or uniform outcomes?
themes.definition: This question addresses the tension between limiting discretion to prevent arbitrariness and preserving case-specific consideration of the defendant and offense.

themes.name: Should intellectual disability, severe mental abnormality, or profound social deprivation restrict a defendant’s eligibility for execution?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how diminished responsibility and developmental or social impairments affect deathworthiness, proportionality, and constitutional eligibility.

themes.name: Does capital punishment remain proportionate when applied to defendants whose culpability or moral blameworthiness is less than that of the most aggravated offenders?
themes.definition: This question examines whether desert-based principles adequately limit death to offenders whose responsibility and offense severity justify the ultimate punishment.

themes.name: Do mandatory or defendant-requested death sentences violate the requirement that capital punishment be individualized and constitutionally reliable?
themes.definition: This question considers whether waiver, autonomy, or mandatory sentencing can legitimately displace individualized judicial and jury evaluation before execution.

themes.name: Do plea bargaining practices improperly coerce defendants into waiving constitutional rights or avoiding the risk of a death sentence?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the threat or availability of capital punishment distorts guilty pleas, trial waivers, or other procedural choices.

themes.name: Do execution methods and execution timing violate the Eighth Amendment because of their risks of cruelty, pain, or procedural unreliability?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the practical administration of executions, including delays and method-specific risks, is constitutionally permissible.

themes.name: Can courts meaningfully reform capital punishment through incremental procedural changes, or do systemic defects require abolition or a moratorium?
themes.definition: This question compares the capacity of safeguards and institutional reforms to cure recurring failures with the argument that those failures are inherent in the system.

themes.name: How should courts balance state autonomy with constitutional uniformity when reviewing state capital-sentencing systems?
themes.definition: This question addresses the proper allocation of authority between state institutions and federal courts in defining and enforcing limits on the death penalty.

themes.name: Do evolving standards of decency and contemporary community attitudes impose substantive constitutional limits on capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines how public standards, jury recommendations, international practice, and changing judgments about dignity shape Eighth Amendment doctrine.

themes.name: Do the penological purposes of capital punishment—especially retribution, deterrence, and prevention—justify its continued use despite administrative defects?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether moral and consequentialist justifications are sufficient to sustain state-imposed death when empirical and institutional doubts remain.

themes.name: Have post-1972 constitutional reforms actually eliminated arbitrariness in American capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question examines whether contemporary death-penalty statutes, guided-discretion rules, and appellate procedures produce consistently reasoned rather than arbitrary death sentences.

themes.name: Do existing procedural safeguards reliably prevent erroneous or disproportionate death sentences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether capital-trial, sentencing, and appellate safeguards meaningfully reduce mistakes, legally excessive punishment, and uninformed death verdicts.

themes.name: How much does state and geographic variation undermine the constitutional uniformity of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether differences among states, counties, and local institutions produce materially different death-penalty outcomes for comparable cases.

themes.name: Does race—particularly the race of the victim or defendant—affect capital charging, sentencing, and execution?
themes.definition: This question tests whether racialized perceptions, victim characteristics, or discretionary decisions systematically influence who receives and ultimately experiences capital punishment.

themes.name: How does prosecutorial discretion determine which homicide defendants become death-eligible?
themes.definition: This question examines whether charging practices, plea decisions, and local prosecutorial policies produce selective or discriminatory access to the death penalty.

themes.name: Does the quality and funding of capital defense representation affect whether defendants receive death sentences?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether inadequate investigation, expert assistance, staffing, or attorney performance contributes to death sentences and later failures of trial fairness.

themes.name: Does effective mitigation advocacy make capital sentencing more individualized and reliable?
themes.definition: This question examines whether developing and presenting a defendant’s life history, background, trauma, and humanizing circumstances changes sentencing outcomes and improves legitimacy.

themes.name: Can individualized capital sentencing avoid producing inconsistent or arbitrary results?
themes.definition: This question addresses the tension between tailoring punishment to individual circumstances and maintaining principled consistency across otherwise similar cases.

themes.name: How do capital juries interpret aggravating and mitigating evidence when choosing between death and life imprisonment?
themes.definition: This question investigates how jurors weigh competing evidence, understand legal instructions, and assign moral responsibility in the life-or-death sentencing choice.

themes.name: Do jury-selection procedures adequately prevent bias in capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether juror characteristics, attitudes toward punishment, and selection rules affect the fairness and legal adequacy of capital verdicts.

themes.name: How do narrative framing and character portrayals influence capital jurors’ punishment judgments?
themes.definition: This question examines whether competing accounts of the crime, defendant, victim, and moral blame alter jurors’ willingness to impose death.

themes.name: Can capital sentencing reliably account for intellectual, developmental, or severe psychological impairment?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether legal factfinders can accurately translate clinical evidence about diminished cognition or mental illness into constitutionally appropriate sentencing decisions.

themes.name: Do categorical exclusions from execution appropriately distinguish defendants who lack sufficient culpability?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether rules concerning intellectual disability, severe impairment, youth, or other diminished-capacity categories consistently exclude those for whom execution is constitutionally disproportionate.

themes.name: Do capital statutes narrow death-penalty eligibility sufficiently to satisfy constitutional requirements?
themes.definition: This question examines whether statutory aggravating factors and offense classifications meaningfully distinguish death-eligible cases from the broader class of serious crimes.

themes.name: Do victim characteristics improperly influence the severity of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether the social status, race, perceived worth, or personal characteristics of murder victims affect charging, sentencing, or judgments about deserved punishment.

themes.name: How reliable are capital convictions, death sentences, and executions in light of wrongful-conviction evidence?
themes.definition: This question uses documented errors, exonerations, flawed investigations, and wrongful-execution risks to assess whether the system can make sufficiently accurate irreversible decisions.

themes.name: Does the Supreme Court’s regulation of capital punishment constrain state practices effectively?
themes.definition: This question examines whether Supreme Court precedents, direct review, and habeas procedures produce meaningful compliance with constitutional limits in state courts.

themes.name: How should national consensus and state variation influence constitutional judgments about the death penalty?
themes.definition: This question analyzes whether changing state practices, legislative reforms, and public or institutional consensus should expand, restrict, or abolish constitutionally permissible executions.

themes.name: Does the actual operation of capital punishment fulfill its claimed penological purposes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether execution produces deterrence, retribution, public-safety, or other asserted benefits in practice rather than merely in theory.

themes.name: Do the system’s institutional failures justify reform, suspension, or abolition of capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question considers whether persistent arbitrariness, discrimination, error, political influence, and human costs are compatible with retaining a state-administered death penalty.

themes.name: Do discretionary decisions by prosecutors, judges, and juries make capital sentencing arbitrary or discriminatory?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the allocation of decision-making authority across courtroom actors produces inconsistent death sentences that cannot be explained by legally relevant case facts.

themes.name: Do race, victim characteristics, and geography produce unequal capital-sentencing outcomes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether defendant race, victim race, victim status, and place-based differences affect capital charging, eligibility, or sentencing, including the disparities documented in studies such as Baldus.

themes.name: Have post-Furman procedural safeguards made death sentencing sufficiently consistent and reliable?
themes.definition: This question tests whether reforms adopted after Furman v. Georgia have meaningfully reduced arbitrary, capricious, or unequal distinctions between capital defendants.

themes.name: Are existing constitutional safeguards adequate to prevent wrongful or arbitrary death sentences?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether requirements governing capital trials, sentencing, appeals, and review sufficiently protect against error, unreliable evidence, and unjust punishment.

themes.name: Does the Supreme Court’s capital-punishment doctrine coherently limit state discretion?
themes.definition: This question analyzes whether Supreme Court precedent establishes clear, consistent, and enforceable standards for regulating state death-penalty procedures.

themes.name: Do capital-sentencing statutes narrow death eligibility to the most culpable offenders?
themes.definition: This question asks whether statutory aggravating factors and eligibility rules reliably distinguish defendants who may constitutionally receive death from those who should receive lesser punishment.

themes.name: Does individualized sentencing reduce arbitrariness in life-and-death decisions?
themes.definition: This question examines whether considering a defendant’s history, character, circumstances, and mitigation produces more individualized and legally justified outcomes rather than additional inconsistency.

themes.name: How does juror comprehension and emotional response affect capital sentencing?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether jurors’ understanding of complex instructions and evidence, as well as empathy, anger, or reactions to defendants and victims, distorts death-penalty decisions.

themes.name: Do sentencing instructions improperly manipulate jurors’ responsibility for imposing death?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether legal instructions diminish, obscure, or strategically redistribute jurors’ moral and legal responsibility for the life-or-death decision.

themes.name: Does prosecutorial discretion explain substantial variation in who receives a death sentence?
themes.definition: This question examines whether prosecutors’ charging, plea, and death-seeking decisions create disparities beyond those attributable to the severity of the offense.

themes.name: Do local legal institutions and state-level practices explain geographic variation in capital punishment?
themes.definition: This question studies how counties, states, courts, prosecutors, and other local actors generate differences in capital charging, sentencing, and execution.

themes.name: Does inadequate defense representation undermine the reliability of capital proceedings?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether insufficient funding, investigation, preparation, or advocacy by defense counsel increases the risk of wrongful conviction or death sentencing.

themes.name: Can mitigation evidence and penalty-phase advocacy prevent disproportionate death sentences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether evidence about a defendant’s life history, family, mental condition, and circumstances is effectively presented and meaningfully considered by capital decision-makers.

themes.name: Can capital sentencing reliably account for diminished culpability caused by mental disability or youth?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether law and practice appropriately treat intellectual disability, serious psychological impairment, and youthful age as limits on death eligibility or punishment.

themes.name: Does proof beyond a reasonable doubt adequately justify execution when residual doubts remain?
themes.definition: This question asks whether the ordinary criminal burden of proof is sufficient for a death sentence when jurors retain uncertainty about guilt or the facts supporting execution.

themes.name: Does capital punishment remain justified when its real-world administration is unequal and error-prone?
themes.definition: This question tests whether systemic arbitrariness, racial inequality, institutional failure, and wrongful convictions defeat the moral or constitutional legitimacy of the death penalty.

themes.name: Does the death penalty produce distinctive penological benefits that justify its use?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether capital punishment achieves deterrence, incapacitation, retribution, or other intended behavioral and institutional outcomes strongly enough to warrant its exceptional severity.

themes.name: Is capital punishment constitutionally permissible as cruel, inhuman, or degrading state punishment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the nature of execution and the state’s authority to impose it satisfy rights-based and Eighth Amendment standards.

themes.name: Can legal reform correct capital-punishment defects, or is abolition necessary?
themes.definition: This question compares incremental safeguards, litigation, oversight, and administrative reforms with suspension or abolition as strategies for addressing persistent arbitrariness and injustice.

themes.name: Do appellate and post-conviction safeguards meaningfully correct defective capital convictions and sentences?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether appeals, habeas review, constitutional litigation, and other post-conviction mechanisms detect and remedy errors before execution.
